Density-functional-theory calculations demonstrate that this stems from weakened local chemical bonds, which soften and slow both acoustic and optical phonons. Reduced interatomic force constants also lead to avoided crossing, further suppressing acoustic phonon propagation. Deformation electron density analyses reveal that the weak Zn-Sb and Cd-Sb bonds arise from delocalized electrons within Zn2Sb2 and Cd2Sb2 rhomboid rings. Benefiting from this pronounced κ L reduction and an enhanced density-of-states effective mass by band alignment, Cd-alloyed YbMg2Sb2 achieves a record-high ZT of 1.4 at 873 K. These findings highlight the critical role of chemical bonds in reducing κ L and provide a design principle for enabling materials with ultralow thermal conductivity through local bond tailoring.
n980e1790c700: The inward diffusion of Ag electrodes and outward migration of perovskite constituents trigger a vicious degradation cycle in inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), severely limiting device longevity. Herein, 2,5‐dimercapto‐1,3,4‐thiadiazole (DMTD) is introduced as a bidirectional ionic barrier layer to simultaneously stabilize the Ag electrode and the perovskite lattice. The ‐SH groups strongly coordinate with Ag+ to establish a molecular barrier against Ag migration, while the ‐N‐N‐ groups bind Pb2+ to passivate defects and reinforce the crystal structure. This synergistic bidirectional inhibition effectively prevents interfacial reactions between perovskite species and Ag+, thereby breaking the chain of mutually reinforced degradation. As a result, DMTD‐modified devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 26.13% and exhibit outstanding stability, retaining 87.68% of their initial PCE after 3000 h of storage at 25°C (15% ± 5% RH), and 80.87% after 1000 h under continuous heating at 85°C.
n0f931627c5cc: Achieving dynamic, in situ switchable molecular recognition in porous composites remains challenging due to the difficulty of precisely modulating interfacial noncovalent interactions at the atomic level. Here, we demonstrated that proton‐coupled interfacial force reconstruction served as a general and efficient regulatory strategy to control adsorption‐desorption behaviors in a metal‐organic framework (MOFs)‐based covalent organic framework (COF) composite, NH2‐UiO‐66@COF‐TpDBA (NU@FC). Reversible protonation‐deprotonation at carboxyl sites induced precise redistribution of the interfacial noncovalent force field, thereby endowing switchable molecular capture and markedly improving the utilization efficiency of interfacial active sites, constructing a stimuli‐responsive adsorption platform featuring molecular capture and release. This atomic‐scale regulation, coupled with solvent‐ triggered microenvironment modulation, allowed adaptive recognition of polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) under diverse environments. Combined with the mechanically reinforced sheath‐tube‐protected solid‐phase microextraction device (STP‐SPME), this proton‐responsive interfacial regulation strategy was extended to an in situ, low‐cost, anti‐interference sample pretreatment system, achieving reliable identification and efficient extraction of trace organic pollutants from complex environmental matrices. Beyond device‐level performance, this study established proton‐coupled force reconstruction as a general design principle for constructing intelligently responsive MOF‐COF composites, bridging atomic‐scale interfacial modulation with expansive environmental analysis.
ndc07e2f31dd0: As non‐precious metal catalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), the performance of transition metal oxides is limited by electronic‐state tuning from static doping strategies. This work proposes a novel strategy for dynamically regulating the electronic state of catalysts using an alternating magnetic field (AMF). We synthesized a series of MnxCo3‐xO4 catalysts, where Co substitution enriches high‐spin Mn2+ centers and introduces lattice flexibility. Under a low‐energy AMF, the magnetic moments of high‐spin Mn2+ undergo forced precession. Through dynamic magneto‐structural coupling within the compliant lattice, this spin dynamics acts as a continuous structural perturbation that provides a pathway for dynamic orbital regulation, potentially driven by the lifting of d‐orbital degeneracy. This optimized orbital configuration enables a favorable binding energy with H* intermediates, accelerating the sluggish Volmer step and enhancing HER activity. Under the AMF, the Mn2.5Co0.5O4 exhibits a low overpotential of 13 mV at 10 mA cm−2, outperforming previously reported manganese‐based oxides. This work offers a strategy to dynamically lift d‐orbital degeneracy for efficient water electrolysis.
n12f180b4a32f: Rechargeable magnesium batteries (RMBs) are a promising post‐lithium battery technology due to abundant magnesium reserves, high volumetric capacity, and dendrite‐free Mg anodes. However, the strong electrostatic interaction between Mg2+ and inorganic cathode lattices causes high diffusion barriers and sluggish kinetics. To circumvent this, two‐dimensional conductive metal‐organic frameworks (2D c‐MOFs), featuring favorable electronic transport characteristics arising from π‐d hybridization and structural tunability, have attracted widespread attention. This work systematically investigates the electrochemical performance of M3(HITP)2 (M = Co, Ni, Cu; HITP = 2,3,6,7,10,11‐hexaiminotriphenylene) as cathodes for RMBs and reveals the decisive role of the metal center in Mg storage. All three materials achieve synergistic dual‐ion storage through heteroatomic N coordination with Mg2+ coupled with anion intercalation. Among them, Ni3(HITP)2 demonstrates superior overall performance, arising from its characteristic Ni2+ d8 electronic configuration, which facilitates the formation of a stable Ni‐N coordination environment and effective π‐d conjugation. It retains approximately 201 mAh g−1 after 1100 cycles at 1.0 A g−1, corresponding to a high‐capacity retention of 98.0%. This study elucidates how different metal centers regulate Mg storage in 2D c‐MOFs, providing molecular‐level guidance for designing high‐performance organic cathodes for multivalent‐ion batteries.
n081921de84bb: Bacterial biofilms are protected by an extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrix primarily composed of extracellular DNA, proteins, and polysaccharides, rendering them highly resistant to conventional antimicrobial treatments. Although natural hydrolases efficiently degrade individual EPS components, their narrow substrate scope, poor stability, and high cost restrict effective biofilm eradication. Here, we report a catalytic microenvironment engineering strategy that enables broad‐spectrum hydrolase nanozymes through arginine‐directed modulation of Zr‐based metal–organic frameworks (ZrMOFs). Systematic amino acid‐directed defect engineering afforded a series of amino acid‐coordinated ZrMOFs, among which arginine‐coordinated ZrMOF (Arg‐ZrMOF) exhibited the highest hydrolase‐like catalytic efficiency (kcat/Km = 1437.5 M−1 s−1). The enhanced catalytic performance originated from the engineered catalytic microenvironment, characterized by increased surface hydrophilicity, enhanced formation of nucleophilic Zr–OH species, and strengthened electrostatic interactions with negatively charged substrates. Arg‐ZrMOF efficiently hydrolyzed phosphodiester, peptide, and glycosidic bonds, enabling concerted degradation of extracellular DNA, proteins, and polysaccharides within the EPS matrix. This expanded hydrolytic substrate scope enabled superior inhibition and eradication of Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus biofilms, outperforming the benchmark enzyme DNase I while retaining over 80% catalytic activity after 60 reuse cycles and excellent storage stability for more than 100 days. Furthermore, a spray‐on Arg‐ZrMOF formulation enabled effective biofilm removal from stainless‐steel, plastic, and glass surfaces, demonstrating its practical applicability for surface biofilm control. This work establishes catalytic microenvironment engineering as a versatile strategy for constructing hydrolase nanozymes capable of broad biomacromolecular degradation and practical biofilm eradication.
n436e2606e35b: Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) are promising for large-scale energy storage but suffer from Zn dendrite growth, water-induced parasitic reactions, and interfacial instability. Herein, inspired by natural nucleotide architectures, we introduce disodium inosinate (IMP) as a green multifunctional electrolyte additive to regulate Zn electrochemistry. Its naturally preorganized nucleotide framework integrates chemically differentiated phosphate, hydroxyl-rich ribose, and O/N-containing heterocyclic regions, which exhibit distinct interaction preferences toward Zn2 +, water molecules, and the Zn surface under different local electrochemical environments. Experimental and theoretical studies reveal that IMP participates in Zn2+ solvation and regulates the local water environment, while preferential multisite adsorption at the Zn interface homogenizes Zn2+ flux and promotes Zn(002)-preferred deposition, enabling dense and dendrite-suppressed Zn growth. Consequently, Zn||Zn cells achieve stable cycling for over 2000 h at 5 mA cm−2 and 2.5 mAh cm−2, while Zn||Cu cells maintain an average Coulombic efficiency above 99.8% over 3500 cycles. Zn||NVO full cells retain 87.3% capacity after 2000 cycles at 4 A g−1, and pouch cells demonstrate stable cycling for 300 cycles. This work highlights how the intrinsic chemical differentiation of a naturally preorganized nucleotide architecture can translate into distinct molecular interactions across different electrochemical environments, providing a bio-inspired strategy for sustainable aqueous electrolyte design.
n6f8e625d26ac: Enhancing electron extraction and suppressing interfacial recombination are essential for achieving high‐performance inverted perovskite solar cells. However, the commonly used [6,6]‐phenyl‐C61‐butyric acid methyl ester (PCBM) electron transport layer (ETL) suffers from self‐aggregation during operation and possesses insufficient functional groups for perovskite passivation, which deteriorate charge collection and long‐term stability. Here, two C60‐terminated bis‐fullerene derivatives, namely C60‐IT‐C60 and C60‐L8BO‐C60, are employed to modify the PCBM ETL. These additives preserve high compatibility with PCBM and feature π‐conjugated bridge‐linkers that can regulate the intermolecular interactions with PCBM as well as the interfacial defect passivation toward perovskite. Compared with the IT‐bridged molecule, C60‐L8BO‐C60, featuring a more rigid and extended dithienothiophen[3,2‐b]‐pyrrolobenzothiadiazole (TPBT) bridge, enables more extensive π‐conjugated contacts with surrounding PCBM molecules and more effective interfacial passivation, leading to enhanced electron mobility, reduced trap density, and accelerated interfacial electron extraction. As a result, the unencapsulated C60‐L8BO‐C60‐based inverted device achieves a power conversion efficiency of 25.40%, and retains 80% of its initial efficiency after more than 1400 h of continuous thermal aging at 85°C in a N2 atmosphere in the dark.
nb023ee68ec93: 2D perovskites, characterized by distinctive quantum‐well structure and high exciton binding energy, offer unprecedented opportunities for photonic detection. However, synergistically driving efficient carrier extraction and rapid radiative recombination within monolithic single crystals (SC) remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, a room‐temperature chemical equilibrium‐modulated crystallization strategy is demonstrated to synthesize centimeter‐scale 2D (PA)2PbBr4 (PPB) SCs. The use of a hygroscopic acid‐base reactive agent precisely regulates the solvent evaporation kinetics, suppressing stochastic nucleation and yielding high‐quality SCs with suppressed light scattering. Consequently, planar PPB photodetectors (PDs) exhibit a notable and robust UV response, featuring a large on/off ratio of 2.77 × 104, a wide linear dynamic range of 159 dB, and an ultra‐low limit of detection of 3.5 nW cm−2. Simultaneously, the intense exciton confinement endows the PPB SCs with strong radioluminescence and robust radiation stability. Both SCs and flexible film scintillators demonstrate excellent practical x‐ray imaging capabilities. Crucially, the absence of grain boundaries inherently mitigates internal light scattering, enabling SC scintillators to achieve an impressive spatial resolution up to 26.5 lp mm−1, representing one of the highest values among the reported metal halide SC scintillators. This work establishes a kinetically control for high‐quality SCs synthesis and provides valuable insights for high‐performance and robust dual‐mode photonic detection.
n1c7b65818183: Efficient photothermal conversion and localized thermal field modulation are powerful design axes for next‐generation energy, electronic, and biomedical materials. Conventional photothermal platforms typically rely on opaque broadband absorbers, enforcing a fundamental trade‐off precluding simultaneous optical transparency and high thermal performance. Here, we report a semi‐transparent Fano nano‐cavity resonator, fabricated via lithography‐free deposition, that overcomes this limitation by operating under a critically coupled, resonant interaction regime. By harnessing asymmetric Fano interference between a continuous lossy background and a discrete cavity mode, the resonator suppresses reflection to achieve a zero‐reflectance (R→0$R\rightarrow 0$) state. Under this coupling condition, the system reaches a balanced 50%–50% optical transmission absorption, respectively. Under continuous‐wave laser excitation, this optimal energy partition drives extreme, spatially confined temperature rises exceeding 500∘C$^\circ{\rm C}$ within seconds, with an internal photothermal efficiency of ∼$\sim$50%. Its functional versatility is demonstrated across diverse applications, including rapid phase‐transition defrosting and localized biothermal tissue cauterization, along with the proof of concept of an optical scalpel.
nef09f75acc62: Practical LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2||graphite pouch cells suffer rapid degradation under thermal stress because liquid‐phase impurity reactions, electrode interphase failure, and cathode–anode cross‐talk are tightly coupled. However, most strategies are designed to address either impurity chemistry or interphase chemistry, leaving the amplified cross‐talk between electrolyte degradation and electrode failure unresolved. Here, we propose a cross‐phase impurity–interphase regulation strategy using p‐Phenylenebis(dimethylvinylsilane) (PDVS) for LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2||graphite pouch cells. The vinyl‐dimethylsilyl groups endow PDVS with synchronized liquid‐phase scavenging and solid‐phase interphase‐forming capability. In the liquid phase, PDVS acts as an impurity scavenger, lowering HF from 90.88 ppm to 29.44 ppm while reducing residual H2O from 10.65 to 8.45 ppm, thereby suppressing LiPF6 hydrolysis and reducing the accumulation of corrosive by‐products. At the solid interfaces, PDVS preferentially participates in interfacial reactions to construct Si‐containing cathode‐electrolyte interphase and solid‐electrolyte interphase on the Ni‐rich cathode and graphite anode, mitigating electrolyte decomposition, gas evolution, transition‐metal crossover, and resistance growth. Consequently, 2 Ah LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2||graphite pouch cells retain 92.81% capacity after 304 cycles at 45°C, show reduced swelling during 60°C storage, and maintain 86.5% capacity after over 1620 cycles at 25°C. This work establishes cross‐phase impurity–interphase regulation as a manufacturing‐compatible electrolyte design principle for thermally durable Ni‐rich pouch cells.
ne1c314ae5e88: To decouple the Seebeck coefficient from electrical conductivity in metallic thermoelectric (TE) systems, we investigated bilayer heterostructures of MXene (Ti3C2Tx) and conjugated polymers with anionic (–SO3– Na+, CPE‐Na), neutral (CP), and cationic (–N+(CH3)3 Br–, CPE‐Br) side chains. Strong electrostatic anchoring between the cationic ammonium side chains and electronegative MXene terminations induces a previously unreported Coulombic trap‐induced filtering mechanism, distinct from conventional energy filtering. The resulting localized potential wells selectively trap low‐energy carriers to enhance the Seebeck coefficient, while concurrent lattice stiffening suppresses electron–phonon scattering and preserves high‐energy carrier transport. This decoupling raises Hall mobility from 1.01 to 5.40 cm2 V−1 s−1 and the Seebeck coefficient from –8.6 to –19.0 µV K−1 while maintaining a metallic conductivity of 5291.9 S cm−1. The optimized MXene/CPE‐Br film, processed with a halogen‐free solvent, achieves a record power factor of 190.5 µW m−1 K−2 and a peak figure of merit (zT) of 0.0279. Strong interfacial adhesion further imparts good electromechanical durability under repeated bending to a flexible TE generator, providing an effective strategy to address the transport limitations of n‐type MXene‐based TE materials.
nfe833c251bca: Mechanoluminescence (ML), which converts mechanical stimuli into light without an external power supply, offers opportunities for self‐powered optical sensing, wearable displays, soft robotics, and adaptive light‐emitting systems. ZnS:Cu particles embedded in a poly(dimethylsiloxane) matrix (ZnS:Cu‐PDMS) represent an attractive stretchable ML platform because they generate strong emission under mechanical deformation. However, most strategies for improving ML performance rely on modifying the emissive composite itself, limiting independent control over postemission photon extraction and spectral conversion. Here, a modular functional elastomer overlayer strategy is presented to decouple ML generation from photon extraction and color conversion in ZnS:Cu‐PDMS composite films. Polyurethane (PU), nematic liquid crystal (NLC)‐loaded PU (NLC‐PU), 4‐(dicyanomethylene)‐2‐methyl‐6‐(p‐dimethylaminostyryl)‐4H‐pyran (DCM)‐doped PU, and DCM‐ and NLC‐loaded PU (DCM‐NLC‐PU) overlayers are integrated as independently tunable optical layers. NLC‐PU forms birefringent NLC‐rich domains that provide visible‐range haze, strain‐responsive optical anisotropy, and broadband, nonresonant photon redistribution. When applied to ZnS:Cu‐PDMS films, NLC‐PU enhances outwardly collected green ML while preserving the intrinsic emission spectrum. DCM‐containing overlayers enable green‐to‐yellow‐orange color conversion, while DCM‐NLC‐PU combines spectral conversion with scattering‐assisted outward emission enhancement. This overlayer architecture provides a deformation‐tolerant route for controlling brightness and color in stretchable ML platforms.
n9fc00713935e: Flexible luminescent solar concentrators (LSCs) are attractive large‐area sunlight harvesters for wearable and portable photovoltaic devices. However, their optical performance is strongly limited by optical losses such as reabsorption and photon escape. In this work, we demonstrate high‐performance flexible LSCs based on vertically aligned tellurium‐doped CdSe/CdS/ZnS quantum rods (QRs) embedded in a polymer matrix. Tellurium doping (2%–4%) in CdSe/CdS/ZnS QRs introduces mid‐gap states, leading to a large Stokes shift (0.70 eV) that effectively suppresses reabsorption. Additionally, electric field‐assisted photopolymerization vertically aligns the QRs, dramatically enhancing total internal reflection and light confinement. Simulations confirm that vertical alignment maintains superior waveguiding efficiency under bending. By further integrating a backside aluminum reflector for photon recycling, the optimized LSC achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 2.22% and an optical efficiency of 17.50% under illumination (AM1.5G, 100 mW/cm2). The device also exhibits exceptional mechanical flexibility, retaining over 90% of the initial efficiency after 100 bending cycles. This work provides a strategy for designing high‐efficiency, mechanically robust LSCs through synergistic electronic structure engineering, optical anisotropy control, and theoretical design guidance.
nccfd9589eaeb: Smart agriculture concerns the precise regulation of light and thermal environments to improve energy efficiency and optimize plant growth. However, current approaches predominantly rely on energy‐intensive active systems or static technologies that cannot adapt to the evolving spectral and thermal demands of plants. Here, we report a two‐dimensional inorganic liquid crystal system in which a frequency‐controlled electric field dynamically reorients nanosheets, enabling dynamic control of both light availability and ambient temperature. The electro‐optic response of α−zirconium phosphate nanosheets is extended into the visible–near‐infrared region through collective reorientation of the nanosheets, increasing the Kerr coefficient by an order of magnitude to 9.49 × 10−4 m V−2. The enhanced response enables broadband spectral programmability within a single device, allowing simultaneous modulation of the spectral composition of light and the thermal flux. The resulting smart window exhibits continuous full‐color optical tunability and achieves temperature regulation of up to 12–19°C under solar irradiation while operating at low power consumption. When implemented in a plant cultivation system, the platform alleviates heat stress, reduces water evaporation, and enables programmable control of plant morphology and nutrient accumulation. This work demonstrates a materials‐based strategy for integrated light and thermal management in intelligent agricultural systems.
nba06ea546290: Mg(BH4)2 stands out as a promising high‐capacity hydrogen storage material, yet its application is hindered by sluggish dehydrogenation kinetics and high operation temperatures. To break the bottleneck, we propose a novel coupling strategy of electron‐deficient destabilization and Mg‐philic catalysis. Specifically, an electron‐deficient boron‐doped graphene host is fabricated to induce charge redistribution and structural destabilization of Mg(BH4)2 and thereby weaken B─H bonds. Meanwhile, Nb‐based catalysts with moderate Mg affinity are incorporated to drive the full dehydrogenation of Mg(BH4)2, during which multifunctional Nb‐based active sites are in situ evolved that facilitate B─H bond cleavage, hydrogen diffusion and Mg nucleation. Benefiting from such coupling effect, the optimized nanocomposite features record‑low temperatures for two‐step dehydrogenation from Mg(BH4)2 via MgH2 to Mg, initiating at 50°C and peaking at 81/144°C, with substantially reduced dehydrogenation activation energy of 38.74/58.86 kJ mol−1. Moreover, the stable Nb‐based Mg‐philic sites enable the durable catalysis for the reversible conversion of MgH2/Mg and suppress the accumulation of MgB12H12 intermediate byproducts, enhancing the cyclic stability. This work offers instructive insights into the performance modulation of Mg(BH4)2 and other complex metal hydrides for advanced hydrogen storage.
n24da6f016b59: Sulfur leaching from metal sulfide electrocatalysts undermines formate intermediate stability during CO2 reduction, yet existing protection strategies remain static. Here, we introduce an interfacial dynamic locking mechanism that actively stabilizes sulfur under reaction conditions. By constructing a crystalline‐amorphous Pd‐PdS heterostructure, the interface triggers electron redistribution from the crystalline Pd core to the amorphous PdS shell. This electron‐withdrawing effect continuously extracts electrons from the Pd core, creating an interfacial electron deficiency that drives dynamic electron buffering. This electronic buffering effect transforms the Pd core into a dynamic electron reservoir, reinforcing Pd–S bonds under operating conditions. Using crystalline Pd/amorphous PdS (c‐Pd/a‐PdS) nanowires as a model system, we demonstrate that this strategy suppresses sulfur dissolution and creates electronically optimized Pd sites favorable for formate production. At an optimal 2 nm shell thickness, the catalyst retains 90% of its initial sulfur and delivers a formate Faradaic efficiency of 77.5% at −0.6 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode, with far less sulfur leaching than a pure amorphous counterpart. Density functional theory calculations confirm this interfacial locking lowers the *OCHO formation energy by 0.35 eV while suppressing CO and H2 pathways. This work shifts sulfur stabilization from static defense to dynamic electrochemical buffering, offering a general design principle for durable CO2 reduction electrocatalysts.
n0fee72197ccb: Aprotic lithium‐oxygen (Li‐O2) batteries have attracted considerable interest due to their ultrahigh theoretical energy density, yet their practical application is severely limited by slow cathode reaction kinetics and large voltage hysteresis. Here, we report an interface engineering strategy to construct ultrafine Ir nanoparticles anchored on Ni‐based metal‐organic framework (Ir@Ni‐MOF) as an efficient bifunctional cathode catalyst for Li‐O2 batteries. Experimental and theoretical calculations reveal the formation of interfacial Ir─O─Ni chemical bonds, inducing significant charge redistribution and downshifting the d‐band center of Ir@Ni‐MOF. This electronic modulation weakens the adsorption affinity toward the LiO2 intermediate, thereby enhancing a solution‐mediated discharge pathway to form nanosheet‐like Li2O2 with intimate interface contact and rapid charge/mass transfer, which facilitates reversible decomposition during charging. As a result, the Ir@Ni‐MOF cathode delivers a remarkably low overpotential of 0.76 V, an extended cycling stability over 400 cycles at 500 mA g−1, outperforming most reported MOF‐based and noble‐metal catalysts. This work provides a promising avenue for designing high‐performance Li‐O2 batteries and beyond through precise electronic structure engineering.
n57a100db8519: Dielectric capacitors are essential components in advanced power electronics, but their energy‐storage performance is constrained by the trade‐off between reversible polarization and dielectric breakdown strength. Although ferroelectric/paraelectric superlattices that stabilize topological polar domains offer a promising route to low‐hysteresis switching and enhanced breakdown resistance, the thick paraelectric layers required to maintain these states inevitably cause severe polarization dilution. Here, we propose a synergistic strategy that integrates topological superlattice architecture with moderate entropy engineering in lead‐free Na0.5Bi0.5TiO3/SrTiO3 superlattices. Phase‐field simulations reveal that local random fields transform continuous vortices into topological relaxor states, effectively flattening the thermodynamic energy barriers for field‐induced phase transitions. This mechanism enables thinner paraelectric layers to suppress remnant polarization while retaining high maximum polarization, overcoming the polarization‐dilution bottleneck. Furthermore, the introduced structural and energetic fluctuations deflect and branch dielectric breakdown pathways, markedly increasing their tortuosity and high‐field endurance. Consequently, the optimized synergistic superlattice yields a superior theoretical recoverable energy density alongside robust field, temperature, and frequency stability. This work establishes a microscopic physical framework for tailoring topological phase transitions and provides practical design guidelines for next‐generation lead‐free dielectric capacitors.
n17f37d9a1844: Gas‐containing triphase interfaces are attractive for oxygen‐mediated electrochemical systems, yet faradaic stress‐induced electrowetting remains unresolved in triphase biointerfaces. This work presents faradaically resilient wedge‐shaped copper nanowire arrays (W‐CuNWAs) that stabilize oxygen‐enriched triphase interfaces during sustained and repeated electrochemical operations. In contrast with conventional passive liquid‐repellent nanostructures, W‐CuNWAs employ co‐programmed structural–wettability anisotropy to reconcile wettable charge‐transfer regions with gas‐retaining regions within a single nanoarchitecture. Compared to cylindrical CuNWAs, W‐CuNWAs introduce shape‐encoded wetting barriers that increase capillary breakthrough pressure by 2.85‐fold and pin the contact line at the upper edge. Across 3 h of continuous bias, 500 potential cycles, repeated impedance perturbations, and cathodic electrodeposition of a high‐surface‐energy co‐catalyst, W‐CuNWAs retain stable wettability and electrochemical responses with only 0.88 kΩ mass‐transport‐resistance drift, whereas cylindrical counterparts undergo electrolyte infiltration and structural failure. The retained atmosphere‐connected gas phase enables Pt/W‐CuNWAs to achieve 1.65‐fold higher oxygen‐reduction current, 8.96‐fold lower oxygen mass‐transfer resistance, and 2.96‐fold faster current stabilization than cylindrical counterparts. Integration with an FeOOH/BiVO4 photoanode enables near‐drift‐free, unbiased photoelectrochemical operation over 8.42 h of repeated cathodic cycling, and reliable detection of Alzheimer's neurofilament light chain in clinical plasma. This work establishes shape‐encoded faradaic electrowetting resistance as a design principle for operationally stable, oxygen‐mediated triphase nanoarchitectures in bioanalysis.
nd90d55465957: Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries are promising for large‐scale energy storage, yet their practical deployment is severely hindered by parasitic hydrogen evolution, dendritic growth, and low Zn utilization. Here, we report an ultrathin (∼5.5 nm) fluorine/oxygen co‐doped porous carbon interface layer constructed on Cu foil via controlled pyrolysis of a fluorocarbon surfactant precursor. This nanoscale interface confines Zn deposition behavior at the Cu interface region, effectively regulating nucleation and growth. The F/O dopants induce localized electronic modulation and hydrophobicity to suppress water‐induced side reactions, while the porous framework facilitates rapid Zn2+ migration and accelerates the desolvation kinetics. As a result, Zn preferentially deposits beneath the interface layer, leading to dense and uniform metal growth with minimal dead Zn formation. Benefiting from this interfacial confinement effect, the optimized electrode, with a low Zn loading of 5 mAh cm−2, delivers exceptional reversibility and cycling stability (>1500 cycles at 5 mA cm−2 with 40% depth of discharge). When paired with a MnO2 cathode, the full cell achieves 88.2% capacity retention after 800 cycles at 1 A g−1. This work highlights a scalable strategy to engineer ultrathin functional interfaces on current collectors and provides new insights into regulating metal deposition via interfacial confinement for high‐efficiency metal‐based batteries.
n48b01139d73b: This review systematically summarizes recent advances in cathode materials for aluminum batteries (ABs), emphasizing the critical influence of carrier properties on electrode performance. Focusing on carrier properties, including ionic size, valence, charge density, and coordination environment, we analyze their transport kinetics, interfacial reactions, and energy storage mechanisms across different cathode systems, including Al3+, AlCl4 −, AlCl2 +, as well as the synergistic behavior of multiple carriers. We identify intrinsic carrier characteristics, solvation/desolvation dynamics, and the electrode/electrolyte interface as the primary factors governing battery performance. Furthermore, the review delineates the constraints of cathode materials in achieving high capacity, fast kinetics, and long-term cycling stability. An integrated framework for understanding carrier behavior and energy storage mechanisms is established, accompanied by a systematic classification of cathode materials, including inorganic, Prussian blue, and organic compounds, together with their corresponding optimization strategies. Finally, universal design principles for structural engineering, electronic structure modulation, defect/doping, and interface engineering are proposed. More importantly, this review establishes a carrier-centered framework that systematically links carrier chemistry, charge storage mechanisms, and cathode design principles, thereby providing a unified mechanistic perspective for the rational development of next-generation high-performance ABs.
n51c2fa868726: Optical information encryption technology has emerged as a crucial strategy for ensuring data security. In particular, the integration of second near‐infrared (NIR‐II, 1000–1700 nm) fluorescence imaging and chemical stimulus‐triggered decryption presents a promising approach for constructing high‐security optical encryption systems. Nevertheless, no related encryption materials have been reported due to the absence of efficient strategies for modulating NIR‐II fluorescence. To overcome these limitations, an organic radical composite MPTCar2+‐MPTCar•+‐CB[8] was rationally designed to modulate the NIR‐II fluorescence of NaYF4:3%Nd rare‐earth nanoparticles (RENPs) through resonance energy transfer (RET), facilitating the fabrication of the high‐security encryption material named RENPs‐MPT+•. This material only generated a fluorescence signal under specific NIR‐II imaging conditions after the H2O2‐triggered conversion of the radical back to the parent compound. These dual‐security mechanisms endowed the encryption material with a high‐level security. Moreover, the combination of this material with permanently fluorescent RENPs‐MPT2+ allowed for the introduction of deceptive pseudo‐information to further enhance encryption security, offering an innovative model for the development of high‐performance advanced optical encryption technologies.
n88f9990a9f15: Mechanically robust yet rapidly adaptive interfacial films are difficult to construct from naturally derived polymers because of their limited structural programmability. Herein, we report an in situ stepwise interfacial assembly strategy that transforms β‐sheet‐rich silk fibroin (SF) and rhamnolipid‐modified chitosan (CS‐RL) into a strong, dynamic oil‐water interfacial network. The resulting interfacial film rapidly transforms from a spherical droplet geometry to distorted tubular shape within seconds without rupture, and exhibiting markedly enhanced dilational rheological properties. Abundant β‐sheet provides rigid hydrophobic nanodomains, while flexible SF chains and positively charged CS‐RL form a semi‐interpenetrating network through electrostatic attractions. Additionally, the hydrophobic interactions between β‐sheet domains and CS‐RL create load‐bearing reinforcing nodes and dynamic polymer junctions, enabling coherent network remodeling and efficient stress dissipation under deformation. This unique interfacial network contributes to stable interface and controllable interfacial releasing and transportation. Emulsions stabilized by this network remain stable after 15 months and show pH‐responsive drug release even under acidic conditions. The network also enables reversible transport of 200 nm nanoplastics across both oil‐water and oil‐oil interfaces. This work establishes a molecular‐topological design principle for creating strong, adaptive, and functional natural‐polymer interfacial films, offering broad opportunities for advanced soft matter systems with programmable properties.
nfc8f51e6c86a: Reducing non-radiative charge-carrier recombination at both p- and n-side interfaces of the perovskite layer is crucial for realizing high-voltage single- and multi-junction solar cells. Herein, it is demonstrated that co-depositing a mixture of ethane-1,2-diammonium iodide and different oleyl-based amphiphiles renders a passivator-insulator modification at the perovskite–C60 interface, which suppresses n-side contact losses in narrow-bandgap (∼1.26 eV) Sn–Pb perovskite solar cells. Interestingly, a cationic oleyl-based amphiphile introduced concurrently with the poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrene sulfonate hole-transport-layer, deposited from an aqueous dispersion in 1-propanol, also reduces the p-side energy loss by providing a substrate for high-quality perovskite films and limiting the contact between the doped hole-transport-layer and the perovskite layer atop. This double-sided interface modification strategy enables open-circuit voltage (V oc) values of up to 0.91 V—over 91% of the detailed-balance limit—for 22.6% efficient single-junction Sn–Pb perovskite solar cells. Monolithic all-perovskite tandem solar cells show V oc and efficiency values of up to 2.16 V and 26.1%, respectively. The results demonstrate that insulating-passivating interface modifications between the perovskite and charge transport layers represent an effective strategy for reducing energy losses in emerging perovskite solar cell technologies.
n8d2770d304fc: A large barrier to replacing petroleum‐derived foams in transport packaging is the difficulty of simultaneously achieving high mechanical resilience, fire safety, and environmental durability in sustainable aerogels. Here, a regenerated cellulose (RC) aerogel is designed via interfacial regulation and hybrid crosslinking: phytic acid (PA) enables phosphate‐assisted crosslinking between RC and polyvinyl alcohol (PVA), while sodium lignosulfonate (SLS) stabilizes the foamed precursor. Subsequent hexadecyltrimethoxysilane (HTMS) chemical vapor deposition constructs a robust hydrophobic siloxane‐containing surface layer, yielding the silanized aerogel (S‐RPPS). S‐RPPS exhibits durable hydrophobicity with water contact angles of 140.7° (outer surface) and 137.2° (cross‐section), enabling rapid underwater compression‐rebound cycling without structural disintegration. It also delivers strong fire safety and thermal insulation, showing no ignition under a 600°C open flame and maintaining a surface temperature below 143.2°C within 3 min. Mechanically, S‐RPPS remains stable after 500 compression cycles at 80% strain (stress loss rate ≈ 6.6% and strain loss rate ≈ 8.1%), retains > 90% oil sorption capacity after 100 squeeze‐regeneration cycles, and maintains performance after one‐month exposure to harsh media. Overall, this work establishes a scalable strategy for multifunctional biomass aerogels targeting flame‐retardant thermal insulation and pollutant adsorption, aiming to mitigate fire hazards and leakage‐induced contamination during transport packaging.
n2d722b852f16: Single‐atom catalysts (SACs) offer broad prospects in catalysis and sensing due to their maximum atom efficiency and tunable coordination. However, the performance of Pt‐based SACs in electrochemical hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) sensing remains kinetically limited. To overcome this, we propose a magnetic engineering strategy that introduces Fe/Co atoms adjacent to Pt sites. Through in situ pyrolysis, magnetized Pt SACs (mag‐Pt SACs) were stably anchored on a 2D electrode. This approach uses the intrinsic magnetic moments of Fe/Co to induce local spin polarization, thereby modulating the electronic structure of Pt without an external field. Compared to PtN4 and Fe‐Co diatomic catalysts, the mag‐Pt SACs‐modified electrode exhibited significantly enhanced sensitivity—by 1.80‐ and 2.14‐fold, respectively. Mechanistic studies reveal that the induced spin polarization generates a net magnetic moment and unpaired electrons at Pt, which optimizes the d‐band center and weakens the over‐strong adsorption of reaction intermediates, thus lowering the H2O2 reduction barrier and boosting sensing kinetics. Based on this spin‐polarization enhancement, the mag‐Pt SACs biosensor achieved highly sensitive and selective real‐time monitoring of H2O2 fluctuations from MSB/VK3‐stimulated cancer cells. This work introduces spin behavior into electrocatalytic kinetics, providing a new paradigm for designing high‐performance SAC‐based electrochemical sensors.
n42d5ff06013b: Flexible thermoelectric has recently attracted great attention in wearable technologies. Ag2(Se,S)-based ductile materials are promising candidates for flexible thermoelectric applications. However, conventional melting methods with high-temperature routes (>1000°C), which are commonly employed for the synthesis of these materials, are energy-intensive and limited in achieving precise control over composition and homogeneity. In this work, a simple chemical reaction route was employed to synthesize Ag2(Se,S)-based materials at room temperature, enabling highly homogeneous distribution and good chemical stoichiometric control. Among the S-substituted compositions, Ag2Se0.7S0.3 exhibited the best thermoelectric performance, and excess Ag was subsequently incorporated to regulate carrier transport. Although the Ag-excess bulk sample achieved a zT value of 0.54 at 340 K due to reduced thermal conductivity, its power factor remained limited. Hot-rolling deformation was therefore introduced to promote an anisotropic microstructure with grain alignment, which facilitates carrier transport and increases carrier mobility. The optimized Ag2.05Se0.7S0.3 film achieved a maximum power factor of 13.88 µW cm−1 K−2 at 340 K. Furthermore, a six-leg in-plane thermoelectric device fabricated from this material delivered a normalized maximum power density of 0.44 W m− 1 under ΔT = 37.4 K, demonstrating the potential of this cost-effective and energy-saving room-temperature synthesis strategy for flexible thermoelectric applications.
n40f4551bf933: Organic–inorganic copper-based halides have become a current research hotspot due to their excellent optical properties, structural diversity, favorable stability, and low toxicity. Herein, we report a low-cost, large-scale synthesized All-in-One (AIO) structural copper(I) halide hybrid material, Cu6I8(bu-ted)2 (bu-ted = 1-butyl-1,4-diazabicyclo[2.2.2]octan-1-ium bromide), which generates broadband green-yellow emission (530 nm) via self-trapped excitons (STEs), with excellent photoluminescent quantum yield (99.38% ± 0.41%) and thermal stability (decomposition temperature reaches 295°C). Its multifunctionality has been demonstrated in high-performance white LEDs (Ra = 91.5), ultrasensitive X-ray imaging scintillators (detection limit: 366.5 nGyair/s, resolution reaches 20 lp/mm), and information encryption labels via reversible emission shifts (Δλ em = 85 nm) triggered by dichloromethane vapor/solution with rapid KI-enabled resetting. This work further demonstrates the excellent properties of AIO-type copper(I) halide hybrid materials and their commercialization potential for multifunctional applications.
n248040d8394e: Brain‐inspired computing demands devices that operate at biological voltages and embody biological principles. Existing liquid‐based memristors offer ion‐mediated computation yet exceed physiological levels and require rigid matrices. Here, we report a hydrogel‐confined electrolytic memristive synapse (EMS) that leverages reversible Ag/AgCl interfacial electrochemistry for synaptic modulation and reservoir‐state encoding at only 100 mV. The device exhibits chloride‐ion‐dependent memristive hysteresis and emulates fundamental synaptic learning rules. Such dynamics provide the short‐term memory and nonlinearity used in a simulated reservoir‐computing framework, achieving 95.05% accuracy in handwritten‐digit classification and exhibiting good performance under noise and mechanical deformation. The device conformability and the design flexibility of the electrochemical interface offer new opportunities toward bio‐integrated systems, promising for adaptive human‐machine computing architectures.
nb392d0a97371: Spin‐dependent pathways play a critical role in the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), yet direct and dynamic probing of spin‐selective catalysis remains challenging. Here we report an optical transduction strategy that provides a real‐time, chemically responsive readout of magnetically controlled spin‐selective OER. A ferrimagnetic Fe3O4/CoFe2O4 heterointerface is engineered to establish a spin‐selective charge transport pathway, where interfacial magnetic coupling enables efficient field‐induced domain alignment under an external magnetic field. Electrochemical measurements and spin‐resolved calculations suggest that interfacial spin polarization favors triplet‐related oxygen evolution. Coupling this process to luminol electrochemiluminescence (ECL) translates changes in OER‐derived oxygen‐precursor availability into a reversible and peak‐selective optical signal through oxygen‐derived reactive species. The pronounced reverse‐scan enhancement provides a chemically amplified optical output of the magnetically regulated catalytic state, enabling dynamic optical transduction of spin‐dependent electrocatalysis. This work establishes a general framework for coupling spin‐dependent electrocatalysis with a chemically responsive optical readout, providing new opportunities for probing and controlling interfacial reactions through spin polarization.
nc668f9fc7689: Perovskite solar cells (PVSCs) have long faced challenges in long-term thermal stability due to their low thermal conductivity and the volatile nature of frequently incorporated additives. Herein, we report a versatile strategy that uses organic–inorganic hybrid filler, composed of 3-methacryloxypropyltris(trimethylsiloxy)silane (MPTMS)-modified Al2O3 nanoparticles, to construct an in situ thermal conduction network in perovskite. The surface modifier, MPTMS, of the hybrid filler has multiple functionalities in regulating the chemical interactions, perovskite crystallization, and intermolecular compatibility. Specifically, it's carbonyl moiety coordinates with Pb2 + in perovskite to passivate defects and stabilize the α-phase, while its hydrolyzed groups enhance Al2O3-perovskite compatibility for the formation of uniform thermal conductive pathways. The resultant PVSC achieves 27.05% efficiency and retains 96% of initial efficiency after 2000 h of maximum-power-point tracking at 65°C under illumination. This work synergistically optimizes the thermal behavior and crystallization stability in perovskite, offering a viable way to improve the thermal stability of PVSCs via complementary hybridization of organic and inorganic functional species.
n87abd45954c9: Reliable recognition of complex scenes remains challenging because physically distinct objects can exhibit similar appearances in conventional intensity images, while dynamically changing environments require continuous temporal information processing. Although circularly polarized light (CPL) provides an additional optical dimension for distinguishing surface reflection properties, integrating efficient polarization perception with multi‐timescale synaptic plasticity in a single material platform remains difficult because these functionalities require fundamentally different carrier dynamics. Here, we demonstrate that donor–acceptor composition engineering in chiral bulk‐heterojunction diodes enables programmable carrier dynamics across multiple timescales. By regulating the balance between carrier transport and trapping, the devices evolve from volatile through quasi‐nonvolatile to nonvolatile synaptic plasticity while preserving efficient CPL photodetection. The optimized composition delivers a photocurrent dissymmetry factor of −0.026, whereas complementary volatile and nonvolatile devices enable cooperative temporal information processing. As a proof of concept, a polarization neuromorphic vision system combining RGB–CPL multidimensional perception and multi‐timescale memory improves static recognition accuracy by 15% and dynamic recognition accuracy by up to 12% compared with conventional systems. This work establishes donor–acceptor composition engineering as a strategy for coordinating optical perception and temporal computation, opening opportunities for polarization‐aware neuromorphic vision and intelligent optoelectronics.
nbaff70d707c5: Second coordination shell (SCS) engineering offers a powerful strategy for fine-tuning the intrinsic activity of Fe–N-C single-atom catalysts, yet achieving targeted SCS regulation remains a formidable synthetic challenge. Herein, we propose a rational precursor-engineering approach driven by the steric hindrance of pyrazole-borate ligands to precisely construct Fe─N4 sites with tunable boron SCS doping levels. The optimized FeN4B3/NC catalyst exhibits an exceptional half-wave potential of 0.92 V for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) in alkaline media and a specific energy density of 967.03 Wh kgZn −1 in a zinc-air battery. Combined experimental and theoretical investigations reveal that second-shell boron coordination induces ligand-field asymmetry around the Fe center, leading to an occupancy transition of dz21${{d}_{{{z}^2}}}^1$-to-dz22${{d}_{{{z}^2}}}^2$ in the Fe 3dz2${{d}_{{{z}^2}}}$ orbital. This reconfiguration of Fe 3d electron distribution fine-tunes the adsorption energetics by forcing electron injection into the Fe─O σ∗ anti-bonding orbital, which generates enhanced Pauli repulsion to weaken the *OH binding affinity and accelerate its desorption. This work demonstrates the pivotal role of the SCS environment in intrinsic activity modulation but also provides an orbital-level design principle for high-performance single-atom catalysts.
na1279452b766: The fundamental trade‐off between structural stability and high capacity remains a key challenge in Li‐ion battery cathode design, especially in cost‐sensitive, large‐scale applications. Here, we present a spatially integrated intercalation–conversion hybrid cathode that combines LiFePO4 and sulfur‐based materials within a monolayer architecture. This earth‐abundant composition synchronizes Li‐ion intercalation with the solid‐liquid sulfur conversion reaction: LiFePO4 serves as a mechanically robust Li host and a chemical regulator that suppresses polysulfide shuttles, while sulfur‐based materials provide high specific capacity. By rationally tailoring the cathode composition and electrolyte solvation chemistry, we reveal how electrolyte–cathode synergistic interactions govern active material utilization, interfacial kinetics, and long‐term stability. The optimized Li‐metal battery delivers stable cycling over 3000 cycles with a low‐capacity decay rate of 0.016% per cycle at 5 C and also demonstrates stable cycling under practical asymmetric cycling protocols. This work provides a new design principle for hybrid cathodes, offering a scalable pathway toward ultra‐durable and high‐capacity Li‐metal batteries.
n53bcca838f3c: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) causes low back pain, yet the causal link between nucleus pulposus cell (NPC) senescence and immune dysregulation remains unclear. Here, we identify that senescent NPCs drive M1 polarization through chaperone‐mediated autophagy (CMA) dysfunction‐dependent NLRP3 inflammasome activation and GSDMD‐mediated HMGB1 secretion, establishing HMGB1 as the core upstream effector of the senescence‐immunity axis. To intercept this cascade, we engineer a reactive oxygen species (ROS)‐responsive hydrogel (TA@HA‐PD‐EVsAR7) with differential release kinetics, rapidly releasing tannic acid (TA) for on‐demand antioxidant preconditioning and sustainably delivering AR7‐loaded EVs for CMA reactivation, enabling a functional sequential intervention. This system degrades NLRP3, blocks HMGB1 release, suppresses NPC senescence and SASP, and restores extracellular matrix homeostasis. Leveraging intercellular adhesion molecule 1 (ICAM1) as a surface‐enriched receptor on senescent NPCs, we construct senescence‐targeted EVs for source‐specific HMGB1 blockade. In a rat puncture model, the targeted hydrogel preserves disc height and MRI signal, reduces M1 macrophage infiltration, and attenuates NPC senescence without systemic toxicity. Notably, senescence‐targeted delivery alone achieves efficacy equivalent to dual targeting, confirming HMGB1 as the dominant driver. This work transforms CMA into an actionable checkpoint and provides a precision hydrogel platform that spatiotemporally disrupts the senescence‐immunity vicious cycle, offering a paradigm for IVDD.
n307dd8794156: High‐sensitivity optical thermometry based on non‐thermally coupled levels (NTCLs) is vital for advanced remote sensing. However, achieving robust anti‐thermal luminescent quenching remains a significant challenge by relying solely on negative thermal expansion effect or defect engineering designs, owing to material scarcity and limited carrier compensation. For this, we propose a novel synergistic strategy that integrates ferroelectric phase transitions with defect engineering in NaNbO3:Nd3+/Yb3+. This approach leverages oxygen vacancies for carrier storage and release, combined with polymorphic phase transitions to modulate local crystal‐field symmetry, effectively offsetting non‐radiative energy relaxation. Consequently, our results demonstrate a 654‐fold luminescent enhancement at 673 K. This dramatic enhancement significantly enhances the fluorescence intensity ratio of Nd3+ ions (498 nm/683 nm), yielding a high relative sensitivity of 4.3% K−1 and absolute sensitivity of 9.38 K−1. These results not only offer a novel strategy for designing thermally enhanced upconversion luminescent materials, but also reveal the significant potential of ferroelectric oxides as promising candidates for high‐temperature optical thermometry.
ne0b594b01886: Three-dimensional vertical phase-change memory (3D vertical PCM) provides a device-level route toward vertically integrated phase-change storage, yet vertical stacking converts cell-level thermal confinement into a stack-level reliability constraint. Here, interlayer thermal crosstalk is investigated in a dual-layer Hf-doped Ge─Sb─Te 3D vertical PCM device by constructing an operation- and state-dependent disturbance matrix. The monitoring cell is initialized in either the crystalline low-resistance state or the amorphous high-resistance state, while READ-, SET-, and RESET-level pulse trains are applied to the adjacent programming cell. READ and SET produce limited disturbance, whereas RESET dominates interlayer thermal perturbation. The amorphous high-resistance state exhibits the highest susceptibility, showing a pronounced resistance decrease under adjacent RESET excitation. Qualitative electrothermal simulations attribute this selectivity to localized RESET heating and transient vertical heat spreading across stacked layers. Paired-pulse programming temporally redistributes the RESET thermal budget by decoupling rapid selected-layer heating from delayed interlayer heat spreading. This strategy preserves the thermal response required for selected-cell programming while suppressing heat transfer to the monitoring layer. Electrical measurements confirm that paired-pulse programming improves post-disturbance resistance retention from <40% to >85%, demonstrating thermal-budget engineering as an effective strategy for enhancing the reliability of vertically integrated 3D vertical PCM devices.
n169c949c3bda: Prussian blue analogues (PBAs), especially low‐cost Mn‐doped Fe‐based PBAs, demonstrate significant potential for power‐type sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs), owing to their open framework and high theoretical capacity (∼170 mAh g−1). However, their capacity decay mechanisms, particularly under rapid charge/discharge conditions, remain insufficiently understood, hindering their practical implementation in high‐power energy storage systems. Here, we systematically investigate the failure mechanisms of Mn‐doped Fe‐based PBAs through multiple in/ex situ characterizations of Mn‐doped Fe‐PBA cathodes cycled under various current densities. Our analysis reveals that there are several pathways induce electrode degradation at high rate: (1) transition metal dissolution that disrupts redox‐active sites, (2) mechanical degradation that impairs electrode kinetics under high‐rate conditions, (3) severe and rapid Na dendrite growth, and (4) interfacial side reactions that generate a thick cathode‐electrolyte interphase layer. Rather than viewing transition metal dissolution and mechanical degradation as isolated degradation pathways, this study reveals that capacity collapse at 10 C is fundamentally driven by the intrinsic kinetic mismatch and mechanical failure, offering key insights for the design of durable, high‐power PBA‐based SIBs.
n99fb3fd3fa1c: Precisely tuning the catalytic behavior of perovskite oxides (ABO3) remains challenging in catalysis, owing to the uncontrollable redistribution of metal cations at the surface. Herein, taking La0.5Sr0.5FeO3‐δ as a model system, we demonstrate that high‐temperature annealing can induce a selective metal cation enrichment at surface step edges, transforming the dominant edge cations from Sr to Fe. This reconfiguration greatly enhances the intrinsic activity (normalized by specific surface area) by 57‐fold for selective anaerobic oxidation of methane. Mechanism studies reveal that Sr cations exhibit a higher segregation tendency than La and Fe below 900°C due to their relatively weaker bonding with lattice oxygen. Upon annealing at 1200°C, surface‐enriched Sr cations undergo segregation and volatilization, which would thereby expose adjacent Fe sites as highly undercoordinated and active centers for methane conversion. Our findings provide the direct experimental evidence for cation‐selective occupation at perovskite step edges, offering valuable guidance for the rational design of advanced perovskite‐based catalysts.
nbdf6ee0e236e: Extreme service environments demand the engineering of innovative high‐performance materials, with high purity as a critical design requirement. Zirconium‐based MAX phases are touted for their radiation tolerance, favorable neutronics, and liquid metal compatibility. Accordingly, they are proposed as highly promising candidates to replace corrosion‐sensitive zircalloy coatings for accident‐tolerant fuels in Gen‐III/Gen‐IV nuclear reactors. However, their potential has never materialized due to their poor synthesizability and thus low purity. The inevitable and poorly understood competing formation of ZrC during synthesis severely compromises their thermomechanical integrity and radiation response. This work combines complementary insights into theoretical phase stability and experimental synthesizability of Zr2AlC${\rm Zr}_2{\rm AlC}$ and Zr3AlC2${\rm Zr}_3{\rm AlC}_2$. Carbon vacancies are predicted to adversely affect Zr2AlC${\rm Zr}_2{\rm AlC}$ stability, whereas moderate (5–10 at.%) carbon deficiency improves Zr3AlC2${\rm Zr}_3{\rm AlC}_2$ stability. Reactive spark plasma sintering ZrH2${\rm ZrH}_2$/Al/C powder mixtures of varying stoichiometry validated these trends: Zr2AlC${\rm Zr}_2{\rm AlC}$ only forms substantially when using stoichiometric or carbon‐excessive feedstocks, whereas Zr3AlC2${\rm Zr}_3{\rm AlC}_2$ formation is highly sensitive to carbon‐deficient feedstocks: carbon‐stoichiometric or ‐excessive (25 at.%) feedstocks do not yield appreciable quantities of Zr3AlC2${\rm Zr}_3{\rm AlC}_2$. Defect engineering thus emerges as a powerful alternative strategy for enhancing MAX phase stability and synthesizability without compromising their chemical integrity, opening new avenues for their design and application.
nc423629360d6: γ‐ray irradiation facilitates controllable, clean, and reagent‐free cross‐linking of polymer networks without side reactions. Leveraging these merits, we precisely tune the irradiation dose to engineer a three‐dimensional (3D) poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) binder network for lithium‐sulfur (Li─S) batteries. By integrating multiscale synchrotron radiation X‐ray characterization techniques, we elucidate how the γ‐ray irradiation dose governs the 3D network structure and consequently regulates sulfur cathode stability and sulfur reaction kinetics without using catalysts. The optimal dose of 3 kGy yields a favorable PVA binder network featuring a dense framework, favorable connectivity, and homogeneous spatial distribution. The interpenetrating structure composed of binder, sulfur, and conductive agent leads to coupling of the mechanical architecture with the electron‐conductive network, accompanied by high‐flux lithium‐ion diffusion, thereby relieving cathode volume variation and promoting sulfur interconversion kinetics. This resulting sulfur cathode delivers a capacity decay rate of only 0.045% per cycle over 1000 cycles at 1 C. Moreover, a 1.23 Ah‐level pouch cell fabricated with the 3 kGy dose‐enabled PVA (3‐PVA) binder achieves an energy density of 390.2 Wh kg−1. This study highlights γ‐ray irradiation as a clean and controllable strategy to engineer binder topological structure, disclosing dose‐dependent structure–property relationships that govern electrode mechanics and electrochemistry.
n3b67de7e5599: Conversion-type anode materials hold great promise for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs), yet their practical rate performance is fundamentally constrained by sluggish reaction kinetics beyond mass-transport limitations. Despite notable advances in accelerating ion/electron transport, intrinsically reducing the large reaction kinetic barrier and activation energy associated with robust metal–chalcogen (M─S) bonds remains a long-standing challenge. In this study, we propose a universal spin-polarization-engineered (SPE) antibonding-orbital modulation paradigm to fundamentally regulate M─S bond strength and enable ultrahigh-rate sodium storage. As a proof of concept, magnetic manganese heteroatom doping into heterojunctions enhances the saturation magnetization by ∼210%, inducing a spin-state transition from low-spin to high-spin configurations, which increases the electron occupation of antibonding orbitals formed between metal e g orbitals and chalcogen p orbitals, and thereby regulates M─S bond strength. Benefiting from this spin-engineered electronic reconstruction, Mn-FeS2/CoS2 anode delivers an ultrahigh-rate capability of 300 mA h g−1 at 120 A g−1, together with exceptional long-term durability (∼100% retention over 13 000 cycles at 100 A g−1), ranking among the best record. The generality of this strategy is further validated by extending SPE modulation to other magnetic dopants. Moreover, the industrial-level pouch cell is assembled to demonstrate the practical potential of this strategy.
nf0ba34601f09: The increasing fire accidents, excessive UV exposure, and health threats posed by bacterial infections urgently require advanced polymer materials integrating multiple safety protections. In this study, we propose an ultra‐efficient strategy to achieve the all‐in‐one integration of inherently flame‐retardant, UV‐resistant, and antibacterial polymer materials through a single biguanide unit. The key lies in the unique triple protection mechanism exerted by the biguanide unit: high‐temperature char‐formation for flame retardance, n→π* transition absorption for UV‐resistance, and disruption of the negatively charged bacterial surface for antibacteria. As a result, the biguanide‐containing polymer material achieves the best UL‐94 V‐0 flame‐retardant rating with excellent self‐extinguishing properties, ≥99.3% ultra‐high shielding rate for UV light, and ≥99.0% remarkable antibacterial rate. Importantly, the biguanide unit is chemically bonded to the polymer main chain, which not only avoids the health risks and performance degradation caused by the additive migration, but also exhibits outstanding heat resistance, thermal stability, and easy processability. This work simultaneously achieves triple functional integration of polymer materials through a single biguanide unit, realizing previously unattainable multiple safety protections against dangerous fires, harmful UV, and widely‐existed bacteria.
n1cb9b1ffcbf7: Touch behavior constitutes the most direct physical manifestation of human intentions, meaning that intention decoding requires human–machine interfaces to simultaneously sense touch position and pressure. Conventional systems, however, rely on physically stacked discrete sensors and von Neumann architectures, causing data redundancy and impaired wearability. Here, we present an in‐sensor‐computing dual‐modal neural fiber (ID neural fiber) that overcomes this fundamental limitation. The ID neural fiber achieves an unprecedented position resolution of < 5 mm and a pressure detection limit of 0.6 N, combined with exceptional robustness–sustaining 300 times load‐bearing capacity and exhibiting < 8% performance fluctuation under bending. Coupled with flexibility, waterproofing, and reconfigurability, the ID neural fiber can be seamlessly integrated into textiles for reliable operation in harsh environments, including underwater robotic control. Crucially, the ID neural fiber enables in‐sensor computing that dramatically increases the information density and allows synchronized feature fusion through programmable logic gates, enabling efficient real‐time intention recognition. To capture touch habits, an intelligent system with the ID neural fiber achieves a remarkable identification accuracy of 98.21%. This work establishes a new material–architecture paradigm that unifies ultrarobustness, dual‐modality, and in‐sensor computing, setting the stage for next‐generation wearable human–machine interfaces with both comfort and intelligence.
ne77e8942d76e: Messenger RNA (mRNA) therapeutics have expanded from clinically validated prophylactic vaccines toward protein replacement and supplementation. Yet mRNA delivery remains centered on intramuscular vaccination and intravenous administration, largely optimized for systemic adaptive immunity or circulation‐mediated biodistribution. Many localized diseases, however, are confined to tissues or compartments accessible by topical, transdermal, inhaled, oral, catheter‐based, ocular, or intra‐articular administration without initial reliance on circulation. For these diseases, the therapeutic objective is likewise local: therapeutically relevant mRNA expression occurs within the affected tissue, and efficacy derives predominantly from the local biological activity of the encoded protein rather than from downstream systemic effects initiated by local expression. This therapeutic paradigm is defined here as Anatomically Accessible Local mRNA Therapeutics (ALmT). The review first distinguishes ALmT from intravenous mRNA delivery and intramuscular mRNA vaccination, then organizes site‐specific barriers and engineering strategies across major anatomical sites. It further examines disease‐focused ALmT applications, highlighting protein restoration, cytokine or growth‐factor supplementation, local antibody‐fragment production, regenerative modulation, and tissue repair. Finally, it discusses general design principles, quantitative PK/PD evaluation, repeat‐dose safety, and clinical translation. Overall, the ALmT framework may facilitate the design, quantitative evaluation, and clinical translation of mRNA therapies for localized diseases.
n047467a7c540: Photocatalytic semi-hydrogenation of acetylene (C2H2) to ethylene (C2H4) often suffers from inefficient interfacial electron transfer from the photocatalysts to adsorbed C2H2. Here, we demonstrate that axial coordination of benzotriazole (BTA) to Ni single atoms in C3N4 (BTA-Ni SAs-C3N4) facilitates interfacial electron-transfer processes. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy, in situ transient surface photovoltage spectroscopy, in situ photochemical infrared spectroscopy, and theoretical simulations reveal that BTA-coordinated Ni SAs serve as the centers for rapid electron transfer by upshifting the Ni d-band center and strengthening the orbital overlap between Ni SA and adsorbed C2H2. Consequently, BTA-Ni SAs-C3N4 achieves a very high C2H4 production rate of 32.29 mmol gcat −1 h−1 with a C2H4 selectivity of 97.6% under simulated solar irradiation, which is ∼4-times higher than that for Ni SAs-C3N4. The apparent quantum yield at 365 nm is up to 4.65%, superior to reported photocatalytic acetylene semi-hydrogenation. This work highlights the importance of interfacial charge transfer in photocatalytic acetylene hydrogenation and provides a rational strategy for designing high-performance photocatalysts.
nd4328196c782: Uniform Li deposition on practical Cu current collectors remains challenging in lithium metal batteries. Despite extensive efforts in facet engineering, achieving homogeneous Li deposition on practical polycrystalline Cu collectors remains elusive, highlighting an incomplete understanding of the structural factors governing Li deposition. Herein, a defect-mediated interfacial engineering strategy is developed by simultaneously introducing a high density of geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs) and enriched <110>/<111> textures on commercial electrodeposited Cu foils. Theoretical calculations and experiments reveal that densely distributed dislocations provide thermodynamically favorable Li adsorption sites and abundant preferential heterogeneous nucleation sites, while the enriched <110>/<111> textures promote Li surface diffusion and lateral growth. This combined effect promotes uniform and compact initial Li deposition, guiding path-dependent deposition evolution and suppressing interfacial heterogeneity. The control experiments further support a key contribution of dislocation defects, while variations in surface chemistry or morphology alone cannot account for the observed performance differences. The optimized Cu foil sustains over 1200 cycles with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.52% ± 0.20% over the final 200 cycles (n = 4) in Li||Cu cells and improves N/P = 0 Cu||NCM811 full-cell cycling. This work establishes dislocation-mediated nucleation and orientation-regulated growth as a design principle for practical Cu current collectors.
n88af105ef95e: Twisted bilayer transition metal dichalcogenides, governed by a single twisted interface, offer a versatile platform for manipulating interlayer coupling and emergent optical behavior. However, despite extensive studies on single twisted interface systems, how multi‐interface twisted stacking influences nonlinear optical behavior remains unclear. Here, we address this gap by systematically investigating the nonlinear optical performance of chemical vapor deposition (CVD) grown twisted trilayer MoS2 (TT‐MoS2) with multi‐interface twisted stacking. We fabricate all nine distinct trilayer MoS2 configurations by CVD. Raman and photoluminescence show that twisted interfaces modulate interlayer coupling, giving rise to stacking‐dependent phonon and excitonic responses. Atomic‐resolution scanning, transmission electron microscopy, and selected area electron diffraction confirm dual twisted interfaces and a supermoiré lattice. Guided by these structural insights, we examine the second harmonic generation (SHG) response across all nine trilayer configurations. Extending the coherent SH field superposition model to a trilayer system with two independent twisted interfaces, we develop a framework that describes how the dual interfaces govern the SHG intensity and polarization orientation across stacking configurations. Our findings establish TT‐MoS2 as a versatile nonlinear platform and open new avenues for understanding and exploiting multi‐interface twisted coupling to engineer nonlinear optical responses in van der Waals materials.
n993902559ccb: The growing demand for microwave absorbers in 5G/6G technologies motivates processing routes that balance matching thickness, attenuation, and temperature response. Here, magnetic field annealing (MFA) is investigated in rGO‐supported FeCoNi, FeCoNiCr, and FeCoNiCrCu compositionally complex alloys at 0, 0.5, and 0.95 T. Among the investigated FeCoNiCr samples, the 0.5 T sample exhibits a favorable combination of dielectric and magnetic responses. Reflection loss yields a minimum of −72.30 dB at 1.59 mm, and a maximum effective absorption bandwidth of 4.40 GHz. At 85°C, the maximum bandwidth is 4.08 GHz, corresponding to 92.7% retention of temperature‐specific maxima. Local microscopy, field‐associated atomistic modeling, and fixed‐composition electronic‐structure calculations support an interpretation of the electromagnetic response in terms of Co‐centered chemical correlations. Finally, flexible antennas and strain sensors based on this composite demonstrate stable wearable responses, validating this SRO strategy from atomic design to device integration.
n89ff613d8293: Integrated visible photonic engines for solid‐state quantum defects provide a foundation for scalable quantum networks. While miniaturization is advancing, active manipulation remains limited by the difficulty of achieving simultaneous milliwatt‐scale visible light generation and high‐contrast modulation. Despite extensive efforts, the concurrent chip‐scale realization of nonlinear frequency conversion and fast temporal gating for high‐fidelity quantum control has remained elusive. Here, we demonstrate a monolithic thin‐film lithium niobate (TFLN) platform integrating periodically poled frequency conversion with GHz‐bandwidth electro‐optic (EO) switching. The device delivers off‐chip green‐light power exceeding 1 mW with an extinction ratio (ER) of 42.2 dB, enabling coherent spin control and time‐resolved lifetime measurements of individual nitrogen‐vacancy (NV) centers in diamond through nanosecond gating. System performance is validated through pulsed optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR), Rabi oscillations, and Ramsey interference, supported by time‐tagged photon counting with nanosecond resolution. By unifying sufficient nonlinear light generation with high‐speed active manipulation, this platform establishes a scalable framework for the realization of high‐rate quantum communication nodes.
nf4363554a3c0: Nonreciprocity reflects the asymmetric propagation or motion of an object in two opposite directions and can achieve directional transport in physics. However, nonreciprocity in natural quasi‐static mechanical systems, including nonreciprocal bending, has rarely been explored. Here we demonstrate nonreciprocal bending in a freestanding ferroelectric single‐crystalline PbTiO3 membrane using suspended‐membrane nanoindentation. The mechanical bending of the ferroelectric membrane is strongly asymmetric in the two opposite bending directions with a difference in effective elastic modulus of up to 33%. The elastic recovery of bending deformation also becomes polarity‐dependent. Such unconventional nonreciprocal bending originates from the asymmetric ferroelectric domain switching driven by the crucial flexoelectricity, as revealed by phase‐field simulations. This work enriches the nonreciprocal functionalities of ferroelectrics and presents a route for exploring more nonreciprocal effects by flexoelectric engineering.
n36bbfe21c9d5: Dion–Jacobson (DJ) 2D perovskites show great potential in stability but do not meet theoretical expectations for photovoltaics due to the random crystallographic orientation in films. We herein report ordered crystallographic orientation of the DJ 2D perovskite, achieved by modifying the intermediate‐phase film with a Ruddlesden‐Popper (RP) phase 2D perovskite based on the two‐step processing method. The introduction of the RP 2D perovskite lowers the energy barrier for the transition from the intermediate phase to the 2D perovskite phase with the ordered alignment, and this strategy is applicable to various organic diammoniums‐based DJ 2D perovskites. Solar cells with oriented DJ 2D perovskite films achieve an efficiency of 21.1% (19.05% for 1 cm2 devices) and exhibit outstanding stability by retaining 98.1% of initial efficiency after 2000 h of maximum power point tracking at 65°C under continuous 1‐sun illumination (ISOS‐L‐2 protocol) and 98.7% after 2500 h testing at a relative humidity of 85%.
n0c66e8980a95: The pursuit of noble metal‐free alternatives to iridium for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is critically impeded by a pervasive activity‐stability trade‐off, wherein non‐precious metals undergo rapid oxidative dissolution under operating potentials. Here, we report a lutetium‐stabilized cobalt oxide catalyst (Lu0.08Co2.92O4) designed through site‐specific electronic modulation, achieving a synergistic enhancement of both activity and stability in acidic OER for proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs). Operando spectroscopies combined with theoretical simulations reveal that Lu incorporation introduces robust Lu‐O bonds and induces charge redistribution that strengthens Co‐O covalency and suppresses Co2+ dissolution, which is critical for improved OER durability, and simultaneously optimizes the Co‐Co distance to favor direct O‐O radical coupling with a reduced energy barrier. Leveraging these structural advantages, a practical PEMWE employing Lu0.08Co2.92O4 delivers an industrially relevant current density of 1000 mA cm−2 at 1.837 V. Separately, it maintains stable operation for over 900 h under a stepwise current density from 200 to 500 mA cm−2, highlighting its potential for sustainable hydrogen production.
n7c7b5c85abca: Globally, warmer lakes disrupt thermal balance, causing hypoxia, salinization, biodiversity loss, and increased evaporation. Conventional floating covers used to reduce evaporation absorb sunlight and warm the underlying water, limiting suppression efficiency to less than the coverage ratio (η eff /Φ ≤ 1). Here, we break this limit by developing Superhydrophobic Radiative Cooling Covers (SRCC) via multi-level structural design. SRCC actively cools the water surface by combining high solar reflectance, strong mid-infrared emission, and superhydrophobicity. Experiments show SRCC lowers water temperature by 2.2°C versus uncovered water, achieving 93.1± 0.1% evaporation suppression at 91% coverage, yielding η eff /Φ > 1.0 for the first time. Large‑scale simulations for nine Chinese lakes indicate that SRCC reduces water temperature by 4.87°C (vs. no cover) and by 12.44 °C (vs. black covers). This cooling could increase annual freshwater reserves by 10.78 km3 across China under full deployment, equivalent to 20.9 L per person per day. Unattainable with conventional covers, SRCC uniquely mitigates thermal accumulation while enhancing freshwater storage, providing a quantifiable engineering solution to climate‑driven water stress and enabling adaptive lake ecosystem management across regional and global scales.
nde086d75db1a: High-energy lithium metal batteries are promising for space, polar, deep-sea, and other extreme environments, but their operation is constrained by temperature-sensitive ion transport, Li+ solvation, and interfacial chemistry. A solvation-equilibrium-locked electrolyte (SELE) is reported by combining dimethyl sulfite (DMS), a low-freezing weakly solvating solvent, with Pyr13DFOB (1-methyl-1-propylpyrrolidinium difluoro(oxalato)borate) as an ionic-liquid co-solvent. Cooperative ion–dipole and weak C–H⋯O interactions between DMS and Pyr13 + regulate the free-solvent reservoir, while TFSI− (bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide) and DFOB− enrich the primary Li+ coordination shell. Variable-temperature 7Li NMR, Raman, and molecular dynamics simulations show that solvent-separated ion pairs, contact ion pairs, and aggregates remain nearly invariant from −60°C to 60°C, unlike the strongly temperature-responsive Pyr13DFOB-free electrolyte.
