n75654fe078f2: Self-assembled nanotubes of C8S3 cyanine dyes have been widely investigated as model systems for light-harvesting complexes. Recently published data point to a brick-layer molecular arrangement in the nanotubes, in contrast to the herringbone structure previously adopted to explain the absorption and linear dichroism data within the exciton model. Here we solve this conundrum by showing that, relying on the brick-layer structure as extracted from cryo-EM, the exciton model can properly account for the observed spectral features, provided it is extended to account for intermolecular charge-transfer interactions.
n95b7a53fbd12: Fluorescence imaging holds theoretical sensitivity for single-cell molecular diagnosis, yet practical performance is limited by residual probe-intrinsic fluorescence arising from incomplete control of intramolecular electron transfer within the probe scaffold. Inspired by natural photosynthesis, where spatially organized pigments enable quantum-coherent excitation transport and precise intermolecular electron transfer, we develop a bioinspired quantum chemistry-guided engineering (BQCE) strategy that programs intermolecular electron transfer to construct molecular assembly based background-eliminating activatable molecule probes (BEAMs). Guided by BQCE, the peroxynitrite-responsive hemicyanine-based BEAM1, despite the intrinsically difficult-to-quench nature of this fluorophore scaffold, achieves near-zero background fluorescence, 103.5-fold activation, and an unprecedented detection limit of 1.3 nM. BEAM1 resolves basal ONOO– fluxes at single-cell resolution, enabling single-cell molecular diagnosis that distinguishes malignant from normal cells based solely on endogenous redox signatures. In vivo, BEAM1 enables detection of lymph nodes containing sparsely distributed metastatic cells, with subsequent ex vivo histological analysis identifying metastatic deposits as small as ∼ 35 μm, extending fluorescence imaging into the regime of single-cell level early cancer detection.
na4e7b22a6d7a: Achieving constructive coupling among multiple second-harmonic-generation (SHG)-active units remains a major challenge in the development of high-performance nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals. Herein, we introduce a coordination-site occupation strategy that enables precise regulation of the geometric arrangement and electronic coupling among three SHG-active components: a delocalized π-conjugated organic ligand, a d0 Mo6+ center, and a localized π-conjugated peroxide ligand. Application of this strategy to a peroxomolybdate system affords three new complexes with progressively increasing coordination-site occupancy. The optimized compound, [MoO(O2)(H2O)(C7H3NO4)] (III), crystallizes in a noncentrosymmetric structure and exhibits a record powder SHG response of 34.9 × KH2PO4 at 1300 nm, together with phase-matching behavior and an impressive laser-induced damage threshold of 5.8 GW/cm2, representing the highest SHG performance reported to date for a peroxomolybdate complex. Computational analyses reveal that the nearly parallel alignment between the organic π-conjugated plane and the Mo–peroxide plane maximizes electronic coupling and hyperpolarizability, thereby giving rise to the exceptional second-order NLO performance. These findings establish coordination-site occupation as a general crystal-engineering strategy for synergistically integrating multiple SHG-active units and provide a rational framework for the design of next-generation high-performance nonlinear optical materials.
nb9b79da11573: The merger of photoredox catalysis with transition-metal catalysis has emerged as a powerful platform for sustainable synthesis, yet asymmetric variants of photoinduced transition-metal-catalyzed C–H activation remain largely unexplored. Herein, we report a visible-light-driven Rh(III)/chiral carboxylic acid (CCA) cooperative catalytic system that enables the tunable divergent synthesis of two distinct classes of chiral sulfur-containing scaffolds from common sulfoximine and alkyne substrates. Through precise modulation of the reaction conditions, the reaction can be selectively steered toward either the annulation product or the ring-opened product with high enantioselectivities (up to 97% ee). This work provides the first example of asymmetric photoredox/group 9 CpXM(III)-catalyzed C–H functionalization and highlights reactive oxygen species as programmable selectivity switches in asymmetric catalysis.
n8b4069e98394: NIR-II fluorescence/photoacoustic dual-modal imaging offers complementary advantages in sensitivity and penetration depth. However, its efficacy is compromised by aggregation, nonspecific binding, and background interference, which persist even with polymeric encapsulation. To address these limitations, we report herein the rationally designed encapsulation-activated triarylmethane dyes (ED5) functionalized with bulky 1,8-bis(2,4,6-trimethylphenoxy)anthracene (1,8-BMPhA) moieties. The judiciously installed bulky substituents not only impart sufficient steric hindrance to repel protein binding and suppress intermolecular π–π stacking but also favor a locally near-coplanar geometry of the conjugated backbone, thereby preserving a high oscillator strength and a large molar extinction coefficient. Upon DSPE-PEG2000 encapsulation, nanoconfinement restricts intramolecular rotation and suppresses nonradiative decay, triggering a marked turn-on response of both fluorescence and photoacoustic signals. The optimized ED5_3@NPs exhibit a 14-fold fluorescence enhancement, a molar extinction coefficient of 71,000 M–1 cm–1, and a photothermal conversion efficiency of 62%. In vivo, they enable sustained high-quality imaging over a 51-h period, achieve crosstalk-free vascular-lymphatic dual-channel visualization, and afford high-contrast orthotopic liver tumor diagnosis against strong background interference. This encapsulation-activated strategy overcomes the long-standing constraints of NIR-II fluorophores, including low molar extinction coefficient, aggregation propensity, poor water solubility, and low photothermal conversion efficiency. It offers a general and well-defined paradigm for high-fidelity deep-tissue imaging and provides a promising strategy for further development of precision diagnostics.
n1e7856d636d9: Catalyst deactivation caused by carbon deposition and metal sintering remains a major challenge for dry reforming of methane (DRM). Herein, we designed and synthesized a Ce-based high-entropy oxide catalyst (NiCoMgAlZrCe-HEO). Configurational entropy stabilizes a multication-disordered lattice with pronounced local distortion, which modulates the oxygen coordination environment and enhances the lattice-oxygen reactivity. The NiCo alloy nanoparticles formed through in situ reductive exsolution are anchored to the HEO matrix, thereby enhancing the resistance to sintering. The reduced NiCoMgAlZrCe-HEO exhibits CH4 and CO2 conversions of 80.2% and 87.3%, respectively, at 700 °C and maintains stable catalytic performance over 500 h. Combined experimental characterization and density functional theory calculations reveal a dynamic oxygen-cycling mechanism enabled by the high-entropy structure. Mobile lattice oxygen favors the selective activation of CH4 by promoting the formation of *CH3O intermediates, thereby suppressing the carbon-forming pathways. Meanwhile, abundant oxygen vacancies facilitate CO2 activation, accelerating the replenishment of the reactive lattice oxygen. This work offers a feasible strategy for designing DRM catalysts that are resistant to coking and sintering based on configurational entropy regulation.
nb76fd2bb038f: Nonalternant polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) incorporating five-membered rings are fundamental intermediates linking planar aromatics to curved carbon nanostructures including fullerenes and nanotubes, yet their formation mechanisms are not fully understood. The detection of fluoranthene (C16H10) in samples from the near-Earth carbonaceous asteroid 162,173 Ryugu and 101,955 Bennu highlights the need for chemically viable pathways under both combustion and astrochemical conditions. Here, we demonstrate that fluoranthene forms efficiently commencing with barrierless recombination of resonance-stabilized indenyl (C9H7•) and benzyl (C7H7•) radicals. Microreactor experiments combined with electronic structure calculations reveal rapid carbon–carbon bond formation, cyclization, and dehydrogenation to the nonalternant framework. This mechanism represents an alternative to stepwise acetylene addition and enables early incorporation of pentagonal motifs during molecular growth. These findings establish radical–radical recombination as a versatile route to nonalternant PAHs, providing a unified framework for their formation in high-temperature combustion systems and carbon-rich astrophysical environments like circumstellar envelopes of carbon stars and planetary nebulae as their descendants.
n46c8d76231bc: Understanding enzyme function requires characterizing not only the static structure but also dynamics and ligand interactions. NMR spectroscopy provides this insight at atomic resolution, yet for large proteins, the difficulty of resonance assignment has largely confined such studies to systems below ∼50 kDa, or to observing only methyl groups. Here, we present an integrated magic-angle spinning (MAS) and solution NMR study of the 134 kDa tetrameric malate dehydrogenase from Ignicoccus islandicus (IiMDH), an enzyme of particular interest as an evolutionary intermediate between allosteric lactate dehydrogenases and nonallosteric malate dehydrogenases. By combining high-dimensional (up to 4D) MAS NMR experiments on sedimented protein with solution NMR, we achieved 92% backbone heavy-atom assignment and 91% assignment of all Ile-δ1, Leu-δ1/-δ2, Val-γ1/-γ2, Met-ε, and Thr-γ methyl groups. Building on these assignments, we used various probes of backbone and side-chain dynamics: elevated MAS NMR 15N rotating-frame relaxation (R1ρ) points to slow motions in functionally critical regions, including the catalytic loop and the mobile surface loop. Complementary methyl-axis order parameters from solution NMR identified additional flexible sites in the hydrophobic core. Chemical shift perturbation experiments upon addition of the substrate analogue oxamate, monitored via backbone 1H–15N TROSY, revealed both active-site contacts and responses in helices α2F and α3G, regions associated with signal transmission in allosteric homologues. The integrated approach demonstrated here exploits the distinct strengths of MAS and solution NMR and provides a comprehensive view of structure, dynamics, and substrate interactions in a large oligomeric enzyme that neither technique could provide alone.
n33ca8e0fbc50: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising polymeric photocatalysts for solar-driven hydrogen evolution, yet their performance is often hampered by tightly bound excitons that suppress efficient charge separation. Herein, we present a linkage engineering strategy that directly attenuates excitonic effects through a facile two-step postsynthetic protocol combining imine bond locking with site-specific protonation. This approach affords a new class of readily functionalizable 1,6-anthrazoline-linked COFs (TP-PACOFs) featuring cationic, fully conjugated backbones with high planarity, tunable donor–acceptor character, and well-preserved crystallinity. Such a structurally synergistic design enables the cyano-containing derivative, TP-PACOF-CN, to overcome the “trade-off” barrier among synthetic accessibility, light-harvesting capability, exciton binding strength, surface wettability, and chemical stability. Strikingly, TP-PACOF-CN achieves a benchmark sacrificial photocatalytic hydrogen evolution rate of 307.8 mmol g–1 h–1 under visible-light irradiation, which is 1.9 times higher than that of its biquinoline-linked analogue and surpasses nearly all reported COF-based photocatalysts. Moreover, it delivers an apparent quantum yield (AQY) of 31.6% at 420 nm, retains activity up to 700 nm (AQY = 1.9%) and exhibits excellent recyclability. Comprehensive spectroscopic investigations and theoretical simulations demonstrate that the ingenious architectural motif of TP-PACOF-CN significantly promotes exciton dissociation and facilitates charge-carrier dynamics. This work provides valuable insights into exciton management in organic semiconductors and underscores the potential of structurally engineered COFs for high-efficiency solar fuel production.
naf5a98af3ee5: The Nucleosome Remodeling and Deacetylase complex (NuRD) plays a key role in regulating hemoglobin expression in adult erythroid cells. Selectively disrupting this complex potently induces the expression of fetal hemoglobin, a proven therapeutic strategy for treating beta-hemoglobinopathies such as sickle cell anemia. In these studies, we have used mRNA display to identify small macrocyclic peptides that inhibit the interaction between two core components of NuRD, the SANT-SLIDE domain of CHD4 and the CR2 domain of GATAD2A. In addition, the screen suggested a second binding site on the CHD4 domain. Based on this observation, we hypothesized and confirmed that CDK2AP1 bound to this region of CHD4, leading us to purify and determine the structure of the ternary complex between CHD4, GATAD2A, and CDK2AP1. The results of our studies show that the SANT-SLIDE domain of CHD4 functions as a critical interaction hub in the formation of NuRD and suggest a strategy to block NuRD function for therapy.
n2c58b2d06982: Light-induced phase segregation limits the efficiency and stability of wide-band-gap mixed-halide perovskites. This work demonstrates that multi-site molecular regulation can cooperatively manage Frenkel defect-pair dynamics, thereby suppressing phase segregation. This stabilization is achieved by thermodynamically suppressing Frenkel defect-pair formation and dissociation while kinetically restricting subsequent halide redistribution.
n6b94715b6b96: The deep integration of human–machine interface (HMI) technology and the Internet of Things (IoT) has imposed stringent new requirements for electronic skin (e-skin) in terms of flexibility, comfort, and high sensitivity. Herein we present a multiconductive network hydrogel e-skin (MCNHE-skin) based on a poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA)/polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) dual-network matrix with polydopamine (PDA), carbon nanotubes (CNTs), and MXene as conductive fillers. The MCNHE-skin exhibits electrical conductivity (<5 kΩ), high stretchability (∼650%), strong self-adhesion (∼19 kPa), and low modulus (∼3.6 kPa). These characteristics enable its successful application in multimodal sensing systems such as strain sensors, pressure sensors, triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs), and physiological signal monitors. Furthermore, by integration with flexible printed circuit boards (FPCBs), MCNHE-skin is developed into smart wearable systems for noncontact HMI. The 0D/1D/2D synergistic conductive network presented in this hydrogel e-skin yields high-fidelity sensing and noncontact control capabilities, marking a significant step forward in the development of multifunctional wearable electronics.
n3656e52b961e: Fluorescence lifetimes near dielectric interfaces depend on molecular dipole orientation, but this relationship becomes more complex when emitters are confined within finite nanometer-thick polymer films. Here, we combine radially polarized excitation imaging with time-correlated single-photon counting to follow the orientation and fluorescence lifetime of individual PDI molecules undergoing rotational motion in thin poly(n-butyl methacrylate) films. Orientation-sensitive fluorescence patterns were analyzed using vectorial wave-optical simulations, enabling dipole orientation and excited-state lifetime to be correlated over time for the same emitter. The lifetime–orientation relationships vary systematically with film thickness and between molecules within the same film. Electrodynamic calculations for the glass–polymer–air geometry reproduce the principal trends and show that the observed heterogeneity is consistent with different axial emitter positions. These results establish single molecular dipoles as probes of finite nanometer-thick dielectric environments.
n49ecbcce489b: Embedded atomic emitters offer a complementary approach to characterizing magnetism in two-dimensional materials by accessing the magnetic environment from within. Here, we demonstrate that ion-implanted Er3+ centers act as internal optical probes in the van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr. Temperature-dependent telecom photoluminescence reveals signatures of the magnetic transition, persistent local magnetic behavior above the bulk Néel temperature, pronounced thermal hysteresis, and redistribution of optical spectral weight near the transition. Upon cooling, the Er resonances sharpen to the instrumental limit, pointing to remarkably homogeneous local environments despite implantation. Measurements spanning a 20-fold range of implantation fluence, structural characterization, and first-principles calculations suggest that the detected emission originates predominantly from an optically active subset of Er centers occupying well-defined environments and minimally perturbing the host magnetism. These results establish rare-earth defects as embedded probes of local magnetism and open opportunities for quantum-optical interrogation at individual lattice sites.
n775542425727: Integrating solar energy conversion and storage into single-unit photobatteries offers compact energy supplies. However, achieving sufficient photovoltage to charge batteries without external bias remains a critical bottleneck for these devices. Here, we demonstrate that the photovoltage in Zn-ion photobatteries can be modulated and enhanced by selecting and structuring the photoactive materials strategically. Randomly dispersed electrode configurations are easy to manufacture but they can suffer from charge recombination. In our experiments, these yielded a negligible photovoltage of ∼0.01 V. In comparison, our proposed layer-by-layer design, integrating a solid-state dye-sensitized solar cell (DSSC) with an optimized spinel Zn–Mn oxide cathode, increased the photovoltage output to ∼1 V under 1-sun illumination. This dramatic performance enhancement is achieved by better control over interfaces and charge transport and establishes a strategy for improving the architecture of future photobatteries.
ne2b86c450632: Nanopore protein sequencing has advanced from a theoretical ambition to a practical technology, overcoming major challenges in protein unfolding, transport and signal detection to achieve single-amino-acid and post-translational modification sensitivity. With both full-length and peptide-based approaches progressing towards commercialization, the field is now focused on scaling throughput and refining analysis tools to unlock a new generation of single-molecule proteomics.
nc78d4c42fe9f: Two decades on from the first atomic-scale devices, atom-based silicon quantum computers have progressed from proof of concept to scalable quantum processors that are rapidly gaining commercial traction. What remains is largely a matter of industrial-scale engineering and 3D integration.
nd96a615d3ec9: As the journal turns 20, we reflect on the journey nanoscale science has undertaken over the past two decades and how nanoscience-enabled technologies have had a real-world impact.
n3b7306b098f3: Quantum dots — semiconductor nanocrystals whose optical and electronic properties can be tuned by controlling their size, composition and surface chemistry — have found commercial success for display technologies. Their transition from nanophotonics research into an applied modern nanotechnology exemplifies the bottlenecks that many emerging technologies must overcome on the path to commercialization.
nb2f1eec7e23b: Curiosity-driven studies of lipid organization and lipid asymmetry in biological membranes led to scalable methods for making liposomes, efficient loading of drugs and ionizable cationic lipids. In turn, these advances led to lipid nanoparticles enabling the RNA medicine Onpattro and the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines, and they are now facilitating gene therapies that can potentially treat most human diseases.
n2dc08f16a75e: Single-atom catalysis has reshaped heterogeneous catalysis by shifting its central focus from surface and interface to isolated atom-centred active sites. This transition establishes a new paradigm for understanding reactivity, integrating experiments and theory, and advancing heterogeneous catalysis from empirical observations toward a more predictive and precise science.
nf1ff5a986198: Spin-transfer torque magnetoresistive random access memory has emerged as a leading non-volatile memory technology replacing embedded Flash in diverse fields including aerospace, automotive and healthcare applications.
nc6aa8f3cb4a1: After years of hype and research, there is still no graphene battery electrode in mass production, but researchers say the material shows promise for energy storage.
n2e47fb53617f: Tryptophan-crosslinked macrocyclic peptides display interesting therapeutic properties; however, methods for their synthesis are limited. Now a Rh-catalysed process enables their synthesis through the development of a dual-function directing group that promotes C–H activation and C–N bond formation. The method provides access to a range of macrocycles, including pharmacophores of micitide 982 and tryglysin.
n30d6e5e89e89: Chiral allylic amines are key building blocks in the synthesis of bioactive molecules. Now a regio- and enantioselective method for their synthesis is reported. The Ni-catalysed process proceeds through homologation of enamines by cross-coupling with alkynes, forming a range of chiral allylic amines in good yield and with excellent enantioselectivity.
nf5a549e04422: Electrolyte cations, long considered inert charge-balancing species, are now recognized as active regulators of electrocatalytic interfaces. This review systematically examines alkali metal cations (Li+, Na+, K+, Rb+, Cs+) and alkaline earth metal cations (Mg2+, Ca2+, Sr2+, Ba2+) in five key reactions: hydrogen evolution/oxidation, oxygen evolution, oxygen reduction, carbon dioxide reduction, and nitrate reduction. We demonstrate that cation effects are reaction-specific, governed by electric double layer structure, interfacial electric fields, local pH, water networks, and intermediate stabilization. Alkali metal cations mainly regulate reactant access, proton transfer, pathway selection, and stability through electric-field modulation, solvation restructuring, intermediate stabilization, and, over longer timescales, catalyst-surface evolution. Hydration characteristics dictate their behavior: weakly hydrated large cations (K+, Rb+, Cs+) enhance local electric fields and stabilize polar intermediates in CO2RR, while strongly hydrated small cations (Li+, Na+) support water dissociation and proton transfer in HER/HOR. Alkaline earth metal cations exhibit chemically coupled interfacial regulation due to higher charge density, stronger hydration, and greater Lewis acidity. These divalent cations facilitate reactions through local pH buffering, water rearrangement, and intermediate stabilization, yet their hydrolysis and precipitation tendencies risk active site blockage and catalyst deactivation, particularly in real electrolytes like seawater and wastewater. By mapping diverse microscopic cation effects onto these five catalytic functions, this review provides a cross-reaction framework for rationalizing apparently contradictory cation trends and identifying the dominant interfacial bottleneck under different conditions. Finally, we highlight future directions in operando characterization, multiscale modeling, multi-ion systems, and electrolyte-catalyst co-design for efficient, selective, and stable electrocatalysis.
n7b16df49d22a: Electrochemical CO reduction reaction (CORR) on copper is a prototypical platform for studying C–C coupling toward multicarbon (C2+) products, yet the fundamental factors governing this process remain under debate. Particularly, how electrolyte composition regulates interfacial proton transfer and thereby governs C–C coupling pathways is still unclear. This paper describes the role of alkali metal cations in controlling C–C coupling in CORR by restructuring interfacial water and modulating proton transfer dynamics on Cu electrodes. By varying cation identity (Li+, Na+, K+, Cs+) and concentration, we demonstrate that cations with intrinsic larger ionic radii in the electrolyte shift selectivity toward C2+ products. Combining differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS) analysis with in situ surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) and attenuated total reflection surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) investigations, it is revealed that alkali metal cations with large intrinsic radii have weak hydration shells that disrupt the interfacial hydrogen-bond (H-bond) network and increase the population of cation-coordinated water molecules at the interface, which may serve as more effective proton transfer channels toward surface intermediates. This reconstruction of interfacial water can accelerate *CO hydrogenation, thus promoting the C–C coupling for C2+ production. These findings identify interfacial water as an active regulator of interfacial proton transfer, thereby supporting a mechanistic link between electrolyte composition and C–C coupling pathways. This work emphasizes the importance of the interfacial microenvironment and molecular-level understanding of electrochemical reactions.
ndb73c3f1a23a: Herein, we report a copper-catalyzed deconstructive oxygenation platform for the direct conversion of unstrained N-unsubstituted cyclic amines into versatile β-, γ-, and δ-aminoketones. The product diversity is achieved by adjusting the substituents at the β- or γ-position of cyclic amines that proceed through single or consecutive C(sp3)–C(sp3) bond cleavage, respectively. Following this method, we achieved skeletal modification of unstrained cyclic amines through ring contraction or atom replacement, leading to rapid structural diversification of cyclic amines. The synthetic utility of this method was further demonstrated by the efficient synthesis of pharmaceutically relevant molecules, fluoxetine, atomoxetine, and norfluoxetine. Control experiments indicated that, in the presence of the co-oxidant nitroxyl, the copper-catalyzed sequential dehydrogenative oxidation followed by single-electron transfer-induced aerobic oxygenative C–C bond cleavage was responsible for this effective transformation.
ne28d65103078: Commercialization of electrochemical nitrogen reduction (eNRR) is hindered by limited catalyst performance, the lack of scalable electrochemical cell architectures, and an incomplete understanding of performance-limiting processes. This work aims to address these challenges through a systematic investigation of catalyst composition and microstructure, device configuration, and reaction mechanisms. Molybdenum (Mo) metal single atoms and clusters supported on mesoporous nitrogen-doped carbon were synthesized with tunable pore sizes via a five-second photothermal pyrolysis of a self-assembled bottlebrush block copolymer (BBCP) template. For eNRR, improved Mo dispersion enhanced electrochemical accessibility, while the coexistence of atomically dispersed Mo species and Mo clusters produced a structurally heterogeneous catalytic environment that benefits eNRR. A gas-diffusion electrode (GDE) flow cell was constructed for continuous operation testing; the catalyst–device system achieved a Faradaic efficiency of 21.6% and an ammonia yield rate of 34.7 μg h–1 mg–1. Intermediate pore sizes and balanced electrode wettability promoted effective triple-phase boundary formation and active-site utilization. Electrochemical characterization combined with machine-learning analysis of flow-cell parameters indicated that activation polarization is the dominant loss mechanism, governed primarily by intrinsic active-site kinetics and electrochemically accessible surface area. In contrast, pore size, metal dispersion, and electrode wettability primarily regulate site accessibility rather than mass-transport limitations. Together, these results provide a framework linking catalyst structure, electrode architecture, and kinetic limitations in eNRR flow-cell systems and offer practical design guidelines for advancing scalable eNRR technology.
ne6813bddcde6: Aqueous zinc metal batteries (AZMBs) have emerged as a highly desirable system for grid storage applications due to low-cost, high-energy density, and safe operating conditions. While AZMB studies often focus on functional mitigation of dendrite formation and the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), corrosion remains a more ambiguous yet crucial limiting factor in anode performance. Specifically, recent work points to persistent chemical corrosion as a major source of resting capacity loss in AZMBs. In this work, we present a wide-ranging mechanism for galvanic corrosion based on fundamental electrochemical thermodynamics and kinetics, highlighting the key roles of battery components, electrolyte conditions, and other contributing factors. Importantly, this mechanistic framework also applies when plating and stripping Zn on the anode, offering additional insight into the ever-elusive mechanistic origins of HER during those operating regimes. We then propose several promising avenues of inquiry and methods for further predicting, understanding, and mitigating corrosion in AZMBs.
n646b78aa0dd7: Triangular metal-oxo nodes are widely employed as catalytic motifs in metal–organic frameworks. Photocatalytic N2 fixation using the all-iron nodes can be switched off by replacing them with all-chromium nodes. However, the two nodes bind N2 in the opposite order to their activity. The present contribution shows that the electronic structure of the metal, which governs the small-molecule binding to the framework, determines the magnetic exchange topology of the [MIII3(μ3-O)] node. Combining broken-symmetry and non-collinear DFT, Hamiltonian-based reconstruction of Mössbauer spectra, and quantitative modeling of temperature-dependent magnetic susceptibility, one finds that FeIII exhibits a genuinely frustrated triangle of comparable antiferromagnetic interactions, whereas CrIII features an asymmetric dimer-plus-monomer governed by unusually strong biquadratic interaction, placing it outside the conventional Heisenberg regime. The distinct electronic structure is reflected in markedly different magnetic topologies and N2 binding strengths, rationalizing the contrasting photocatalytic activities of the two frameworks. These results establish magnetic exchange topology as an experimentally accessible descriptor of chemical function in trinuclear MOF nodes.
n665c5f02f781: Coordinated delivery of therapeutics with distinct physicochemical properties remains a fundamental challenge in drug design. This difficulty often stems from incompatible assembly kinetics, in which mismatched assembly behaviors among components lead to disordered structures and hinder functional integration. Here, we report a cascade assembly strategy to construct core–shell microassemblies (MTX@HPTD) by capturing transient intermediate states, enabling sequential structural organization and functional integration for spatiotemporal drug release. Upon solvent exchange, methotrexate (MTX) and phenylboronic acid-modified hyaluronic acid (HP) coassemble, thereby allowing the capture of an intermediate in which a dense MTX-rich core forms while the surrounding HP shell remains accessible for subsequent integration. This enables covalent anchoring of ROS-scavenging TEMPO-doped polydopamine nanoparticles (TPDA) into the evolving shell of the intermediate assembly via dynamic covalent bonding. The resulting core–shell microassemblies, featuring an MTX-rich reservoir stabilized by a functionalized HP-rich shell that entraps the TPDA payload, exhibit spatially segregated compartments, enabling diffusion-controlled release of MTX and stimuli-responsive release of TPDA. Moreover, by utilizing changes in the size of microassemblies during release, this system addresses the size-dependent trade-off between retention and uptake. In a psoriasis model, microneedle-mediated delivery achieves coordinated therapy, suppressing ferroptosis, necroptosis, and HMGB1 signaling, thereby mitigating disease severity. This work establishes the temporal capture of transient states as a promising strategy for constructing hierarchical materials for spatiotemporal release.
n772293ee5006: Performance of tandem junction nanowire (NW) solar cells relies on the electronic quality of the tunnel diodes which serve as the separating junctions between subcells. Yet, the relevant interfacial physics occurs below the optical diffraction limit. Here we use hyperspectral tip-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (TERS) to map, with nanoscale precision, axially defined heterojunctions in InP/InGaP tandem junction photovoltaic NWs. By resolving mode-specific phonon and phonon–plasmon responses, we show that the nominally abrupt p/p++ and p++/n++ junctions are compositionally graded. The TOM mode, used as the primary compositional marker, yields transition widths of ∼90–120 nm, whereas other lattice- and carrier-sensitive modes exhibit broader central widths up to ∼190 nm, reflecting their additional sensitivity to alloying, structural disorder, and electronic coupling. In a first-order approximation, rescaling these TERS-derived widths to shorter, device-relevant NWs yields narrower junctions, consistent with independent Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) measurements that qualitatively capture the same trend despite surface and tip convolution effects. Complementary equilibrium band-edge model combined with a simplified one-dimensional Wentzel–Kramers–Brillouin (WKB) calculation, as an illustrative trend, further indicates that such grading is expected to widen the effective tunnel barrier. These findings establish mode-selective hyperspectral TERS as a validated, noninvasive method for quantitative nanoscale mapping of compositional grading in III–V NW junctions, with the carrier-sensitive L1 phonon–plasmon response providing complementary, model-assisted insight into the electronic evolution of the junctions.
n88759cb66d56: All-solid-state Li batteries operating at high current densities exceeding 10 mA cm–2 are desired for high-power and rapid-charging batteries. Therefore, battery development needs to focus on reducing the electrolyte–electrode interface resistance at high current density, which is a major contributor to internal resistance. However, methods for reducing the electrolyte–electrode interfacial resistance at high current densities remain unexplored. Here, we demonstrate charge–discharge operation at 30 mA cm–2 using Li3PS4, LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, and Li metal as a solid electrolyte, 5 V-class positive electrode, and negative electrode, respectively. The introduction of Li3PO4 buffer layers at both Li–Li3PS4 and Li3PS4–LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4 interfaces reduced the interfacial resistance 45,000-fold. Furthermore, the introduction of a 5 nm-thick Pt layer instead of Li3PO4 at the Li–Li3PS4 interface enabled charge–discharge operation under high-current-density conditions. This quantitative study highlights the importance of designing electrochemically robust negative electrode and electrolyte interfaces for high-power 5 V-class all-solid-state Li batteries.
n1448593c37d1: Fe-containing Ni oxyhydroxides are among the most active alkaline oxygen evolution catalysts, whose structures and performances strongly depend on precursor reconstruction and Fe location. However, achieving precise control over precursor design, reconstruction, and Fe incorporation remains highly challenging. Here, we report the low-temperature synthesis of intermetallic Ni2In3 nanoparticles as a precursor and uncover their in situ reconstruction behavior modulated by electrolyte concentration. Compared with similarly sized Ni nanoparticle-derived catalysts, the Ni2In3-derived catalysts exhibit significantly enhanced activity and stability. The optimal catalyst, after activation in 6 M KOH with Fe spiking, requires an overpotential of only 284 mV for 10 mA cm–2, along with a low Tafel slope of 31 mV dec–1. Combined electrochemical analyses, in situ/ex situ characterizations, and theoretical calculations reveal that In leaching induces electronic structure modulation and surface undercoordinated site enrichment, thereby facilitating interfacial Fe incorporation to form NiFe active centers. In an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer, the catalyst demonstrates excellent stability of 260 h at 1 A cm–2 at 80 °C. These findings highlight the importance of electrolyte- and precursor-dependent reconstruction in modulating the electronic structure and promoting interfacial Fe incorporation, thereby enabling the design of oxygen evolution electrocatalysts.
n328fe8e09ea3: Hyperlactatemia is a critical indicator of tissue hypoperfusion, metabolic dysfunction, and an adverse prognosis in critically ill patients. Yet conventional monitoring depends entirely on intermittent, invasive blood sampling, which cannot capture the dynamic metabolic fluctuations required to guide timely clinical interventions. Herein, we report a wearable sweat-sensing device built on a dual-diffusion-limiting architecture for the continuous and accurate assessment of clinical hyperlactatemia. This system synergistically modulates lactate diffusion in sweat through a silane-network-encapsulated lactate oxidase layer coupled to a polyvinyl chloride layer. This design effectively delays enzyme saturation, extending the linear detection range for sweat lactate to 0–60 mM and thereby fulfilling the stringent requirements of critical care monitoring. The device also integrates real-time pH and temperature calibration to safeguard measurement accuracy in complex physiological environments. Moreover, linear mixed-effects analysis of 82 paired samples from 33 critically ill patients demonstrated a strong association between sweat and blood lactate levels, with a marginal R2 of 0.840. Sweat lactate effectively identified hyperlactatemia and predicted in-hospital mortality, yielding areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve values of 0.943 and 0.785, respectively. The integrated iontophoresis-microfluidics module further ensures high consistency with bedside arterial blood gas analysis, as validated by a marginal R2 of 0.811. Together, these results establish sweat biosensors as a promising platform for continuous metabolic monitoring, resuscitation assessment, and objective prognostic stratification in critical care settings.
n12e162a45ea9: Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries promise large‐scale storage, yet anode irreversibility remains the principal barrier. Eutectic electrolytes, comprising hydrogen‐bond donors (HBDs) and acceptors (HBAs), can suppress H2O activity and regulate Zn2+ desolvation through hydrogen‐bond networks, offering a promising remedy. However, the screening of polyol‐based HBDs still relies on empirical trials, lacking quantitative molecular criteria. Herein, two orthogonal descriptors, effective hydroxyl density (EOD) and minimum electrostatic potential (MEP), are proposed based on the saturation and directionality of hydrogen bonds to evaluate polyols from two aspects of hydrogen‐bond network formation and Zn2+ coordination. A series of C2–C6 polyols are explored for hydrated eutectic electrolytes, revealing inconsistency between bulk hydrogen‐bond strength and battery performance. Erythritol (Ery, C4, EOD = 0.022 Å−3, MEP = −1.73 eV) optimizes interfacial adsorption stability and desolvation kinetics. It constructs an Ery‐enriched interfacial layer to induce preferred (101) Zn texture. The symmetric cell stably cycles over 6740 h at 2 mA cm−2 with 1 mAh cm−2, and the Zn||I2 full cell exhibited 11 400 cycles at 10 C. This work establishes theoretical design principles for the selection of polyol HBDs when keeping the HBA component fixed as a zinc salt, shifting the paradigm from trial and error to rational design.
nc143c8fe2741: Low‐frequency, random, and intermittent vibrational energy is an important energy source for self‐powered sensing systems in engineering environments. However, the high dependence of triboelectric nanogenerators on periodic excitation limits their continuous energy output. Here, a gravity‐differential modulated triboelectric nanogenerator (GDM‐TENG) is proposed to transform intermittent vibrations into a continuously enhanced energy conversion process. Through the synergistic effect of mechanical rectification, inertial energy storage, gravity‐driven propulsion, and differential motion amplification, the GDM‐TENG directionally transmits and delays the release of discrete vibrational inputs, thereby forming a more continuous and higher‐frequency relative sliding motion at the triboelectric interface and improving the effective charge transfer rate per unit time. Compared to the single pendulum system, the double‐sided pendulum shortens the energy storage time by 64.2%, compressing the energy response to the millisecond level, while increasing output power by 2.81 times and capacitor charging rate by 2.55 times. After 216,000 cycles, the voltage output of the GDM‐TENG remains almost unchanged, indicating its excellent long‐term operational stability. Furthermore, combined with a power management circuit, the GDM‐TENG can stably charge a 1000 µF capacitor and power warning lights and acoustic flame sensors. This work provides a design idea for distributed self‐powered sensing systems toward the infrastructure monitoring.
n1ef0f4423759: Piezo-photoelectrochemical (Piezo-PEC) water splitting enables efficient solar conversion, yet its practical implementation is limited by an insufficient piezoelectric polarization field and sluggish water-splitting kinetics. Herein, we firstly propose a Jahn–Teller effect-driven strategy to regulate the local B-site octahedral structure of perovskite BaTiO3 for efficient Piezo-PEC water splitting. By introducing Mn3+ ions with asymmetric eg orbital occupancy (t2g 3eg 1), a local MnO6 octahedral coordination environment is constructed and pronounced Jahn–Teller distortion is induced. Experimental characterizations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the Jahn–Teller distortion drives the cooperative displacement of Ti and O atoms and enhances crystal non-centrosymmetry, thereby generating a stronger piezoelectric polarization field under mechanical stress. Meanwhile, the introduction of Mn3+ strengthens Ti─O bond covalency, thereby activating lattice oxygen species and promoting the water-splitting pathway from the conventional adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) toward the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM), thus accelerating reaction kinetics. Under coupled ultrasonic vibration and illumination, the optimized BTMO-6 photoanode delivers a high photocurrent density of 2.18 mA cm−2 at 1.23 VRHE and exhibits a piezoelectric coefficient (d33) of 52.3 pm V−1. This work reveals that Jahn–Teller distortion simultaneously enhances piezo-polarization and tunes reaction pathways, offering new insights for robust Piezo-PEC water-splitting systems.
n73e54754107f: High‐efficiency organic solar cells require optimal donor‐acceptor heterojunctions to facilitate efficient charge generation, separation, and collection. These bulk‐heterojunction (BHJ) blends are typically kinetically quenched in nonequilibrium morphologies, contributing to device degradation over time. Yet how acceptor molecules govern homo‐ and hetero‐intermolecular interactions to confer thermal stability to BHJ blends remains elusive. Herein, we present experimental and theoretical studies of 28 distinct non‐fullerene acceptors (NFAs) to elucidate the relationships between molecular structure, intermolecular interaction, and morphological stability of BHJ blends, covering the well‐known indacenodithieno[3,2‐b]thiophene‐based (ITIC‐series) acceptors, indacenodithiophene‐based (IEICO‐series) acceptors, and state‐of‐the‐art Y‐series and dimer/trimer acceptors. We demonstrate that structural modifications of NFAs not only modulate the homo‐interaction energies between acceptor molecules but also fine‐tune their hetero‐interaction energies with donors, thereby governing the stability of BHJ nanostructures. Thermally stable BHJ blends necessitate strong homo‐interactions while minimizing hetero‐interactions to suppress NFA diffusion within the blends. The proposed intermolecular interaction effect on thermal stability is further validated by 13 literature‐reported NFA blends, demonstrating the broad applicability. These findings underscore the pivotal role of NFA structural engineering in regulating intermolecular interactions and offer valuable insights into balancing homo‐ and hetero‐interactions for the rational molecular design of thermally stable organic semiconductor blends.
nf206820a8784: High efficiency inverted perovskite solar cells often rely on nickel‐containing hole‐selective interfaces such as NiOx. However, the use of nickel presents sustainability challenges, as the material is inherently toxic and cross‐contamination during end‐of‐life processing can compromise material recovery and recyclability. Here, we develop a nickel‐free hole‐selective interface material based on phenyl‐substituted phosphonic‐acid carbazole self‐assembled monolayers (Ph‐nPACz). Candidate molecules were identified through rational structure‐property screening of the substituents of the carbazole core, anchoring groups and linkers. Among this molecular family, Ph‐5PACz delivers the best overall performance, offering improved interfacial wettability and enhanced buried‐interface stability compared to the NiOx/Me‐4PACz reference. Devices incorporating Ph‐5PACz achieve a power conversion efficiency of 25.3%, compared to 21.7% for the control, driven by a higher fill factor and efficient charge extraction. The chemical robustness of the nickel‐free interface enables a closed‐loop recycling route unavailable to nickel‐based devices, with recycled‐ITO devices retaining close to 98% of their initial performance. Coupled life‐cycle and techno‐economic analyses further indicate substantial sustainability gains, including reduced energy demand, markedly lower raw metal usage and toxicity‐related impacts, and a generalized reduction of up to 29% across ReCiPe endpoint indicators.
nb4a64af6ed02: Photoelectrochemical reduction of nitrate to ammonia (PEC NO3RR) offers a solar‐driven route to NH3 synthesis under ambient conditions, converting an environmental pollutant into a value‐added product. However, the overall performance of a PEC photoelectrode has been largely governed by the cocatalyst deposited on the light absorber since NO3RR conversion is kinetically demanding. Electrochemical NO3RR research has produced an extensive library of high‐performance catalysts together with a mature mechanistic understanding. Yet this knowledge has rarely been translated into photoelectrode design. This review summarizes recent advances in PEC NO3RR, spanning light‐absorber engineering, photoelectrode–cocatalyst integration, intrinsic semiconductor catalytic activity, and architectures that decouple light absorption from catalysis. On this basis, we reframe the electrochemical NO3RR catalyst library as a design resource for PEC cocatalysts and identify key evaluation criteria, such as catalytic activity, interfacial charge‐transfer, optical shading, and stability under illumination and electrically biased conditions. By bridging the mechanistic maturity of electrochemistry with the energetic advantages of photoelectrochemistry, this review provides a coherent design framework for advancing PEC NH3 synthesis.
ncf574fda2631: Selective photocatalytic reduction of CO2 into multicarbon products remains challenging because constructing uniform C─C coupling centers while maintaining their stability under reaction conditions is difficult. Here, we report a Z‐scheme CuWO4/poly(heptazine imide) heterojunction featuring asymmetric Cu2+/Cu+ dual sites for CO2‐to‐ethanol conversion. Site‐selective oxygen vacancies in CuWO4 trigger generation of structurally identical, charge‐asymmetric neighboring Cu sites, which enhance CO2 activation and stabilize adjacent *CO intermediates, thereby facilitating C─C bond formation. Meanwhile, an atomically bonded O─W─N heterointerface enables directional Z‐scheme charge transfer, supplying photogenerated electrons to the CuWO4 surface and stabilizing the asymmetric Cu2+/Cu+ dual sites throughout photocatalysis. Consequently, the optimized photocatalyst achieves an ethanol production rate of 244.5 µmol g−1 h−1 in pure water without sacrificial reagents. Advanced synchrotron spectroscopies identify the asymmetric Cu2+/Cu+ dual sites and the chemically bonded heterointerface, while operando spectroscopies record the dynamic evolution of active sites and the *CO─*CO coupling pathways upon illumination. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the synergy between asymmetric catalytic centers and the atomically bonded heterointerface promotes the C─C coupling process. This work establishes a strategy for constructing and stabilizing asymmetric catalytic centers through atomic engineering of crystal structure and heterointerface, providing a photocatalyst design paradigm for selective multicarbon solar fuel synthesis.
nb435aa966562: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising nanophotosensitizers for photodynamic therapy (PDT), but most reported systems rely predominantly on a single O2‐activation pathway, limiting their ability to produce complementary reactive oxygen species (ROS). Herein, we report a bifunctional MOF, Hf‐VIO‐DBP, that integrates porphyrinic photosensitizers (DBP) and viologen electron mediators (VIO2+) within a single framework to establish a dual‐channel photoactive platform. The close spatial proximity of these two functional units enables efficient intra‐framework electron transfer while preserving the energy transfer capability of the porphyrinic photosensitizers. Upon 630 nm irradiation, excited DBP transfers electrons to VIO2+ to generate viologen radical species, which mediate O2 reduction to generate type I ROS, including superoxide, hydrogen peroxide, and hydroxyl radicals. The resulting DBP radical cation is reduced by endogenous biomolecules such as 1,4‐dihydronicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, thereby regenerating DBP and sustaining the photoredox cycle. Concurrently, energy transfer from excited DBP to O2 produces singlet oxygen through a type II pathway. Compared with the viologen‐free MOF analogue, Hf‐VIO‐DBP markedly enhances type I ROS generation while retaining efficient type II ROS production, resulting in substantially improved overall ROS yields and phototoxicity. Therefore, Hf‐VIO‐DBP achieves potent PDT efficacy in CT26 and MC38 murine colon cancer models.
nc849f363f339: Vitamin C is an essential micronutrient, yet its direct chemical engagement with the proteome remains poorly defined. Here, we develop and experimentally benchmark a bioorthogonal probe platform for labeling, profiling, and imaging of lysine vitcylation, a recently identified vitamin C‐derived post‐translational modification, in living cells. Chemoproteomic analysis and fluorescence imaging reveal a candidate vitcylome enriched in nucleolar proteins associated with ribonucleoprotein biogenesis and RNA processing, and reporter‐derived lysine adducts on selected targets were validated by mass spectrometry. Time‐resolved analyses demonstrate that intracellular vitcylation undergoes unexpectedly rapid remodeling, indicating active cellular regulation. Furthermore, a genome‐wide CRISPR‐Cas9 screen identifies glutathione S‐transferase P1 (GSTP1) as an upstream regulator of global vitamin C‐derived protein modification, linking vitcylation remodeling to cellular electrophile handling and redox homeostasis. Collectively, this platform provides a chemical framework for profiling, visualizing, and investigating protein vitcylation in living cells, and reveals vitcylation as a dynamic, spatially organized and regulated metabolic modification.
nf1d867eafa59: All previously reported Ge(II) dications have remained chemically dormant, their reactivity confined to simple coinage metal coordination—a consequence of cationization‐induced lone pair contraction that renders the Ge center inaccessible to substrates. We report that dual σ/π‐donating carbodicarbene (CDC) ligands directly counteract this contraction, yielding [(CDC)2Ge][OTf]2 (4), the first two‐coordinate Ge(II) dication to display broad reactivity beyond coinage metal coordination. Crystallographic and computational analysis reveal a delocalized 3c‐4e C‐Ge‐C moiety and a less contracted Ge lone pair with retained Ge‐centered LUMO, underpinning an unprecedented reactivity profile encompassing 1,1‐oxidative addition, [1 + 4] cycloaddition, selenium insertion, and cooperative C–S bond activation. As a Ge‐donor ligand, 4 coordinates to Rh, Ir, and Ag with donor strength comparable to that of IMes and forms geminal bimetallic complex 8, featuring a rare noncluster Ag–Ge–Ag three‐center two‐electron bonding motif. These results establish CDC‐based low‐coordination stabilization as a productive strategy for accessing structurally simple yet reactive main‐group dications.
n63e4c6aae79d: Interfacial electronic coupling plays a decisive role in governing excited‐state evolution and signal transduction in optoelectronic systems, yet dynamically adaptive interfaces driven by valence‐state evolution remain largely unexplored in fluorescent sensing platforms. Herein, an Eu‐functionalized Ce‐MOF/CTF heterointerface is constructed to establish a valence‐responsive optoelectronic system for dual‐mode H2O2 sensing. Upon oxidative stimulation, the Ce‐MOF/CTF heterointerface dynamically reconstructs the interfacial charge‐transfer network through Ce3+/Ce4+ valence‐state evolution, enabling modulation of electron migration across the interface and synchronously regulating Eu‐centered luminescence, CTF‐derived fluorescence, and nanozyme‐mediated catalytic outputs. The results reveal that oxidative valence evolution induces adaptive interfacial electronic redistribution and excited‐state pathway reconstruction, thereby amplifying microscopic electronic perturbations into programmable fluorescence–catalytic responses. Beyond conventional sensing systems dominated by static emissive centers, this work demonstrates that adaptive interface states can function as dynamic optoelectronic units for intelligent signal transduction. Furthermore, the interfacial optical response can be integrated into flexible electrospun membranes and machine‐learning‐assisted visual recognition systems, enabling portable dual‐mode visual sensing. This work provides a new perspective for constructing adaptive optoelectronic interfaces through valence‐state engineering and establishes a general framework for next‐generation intelligent sensing platforms.
n007432bcf39f: Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) is an important oxidant for chemical manufacturing, environmental remediation, and biomedical applications, yet its industrial production still relies mainly on the energy‐intensive anthraquinone process. Electrochemical H2O2 synthesis via the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e− ORR) provides a sustainable alternative but is often hindered by sluggish charge transport and insufficient O2 activation. Here, we develop a bond‐hybridization strategy by incorporating sp‐hybridized acetylene units into the vertex or linker of covalent organic frameworks (COFs). The resulting COFs feature extended π‐conjugation, enhanced charge delocalization, and electronically polarized pores, thereby strengthening O2 adsorption and activation. Compared with sp2‐dominated analogues, these sp‐hybridized COFs show faster charge‐transfer kinetics, higher H2O2 selectivity, and improved 2e− ORR activity. In a flow cell, the optimized catalyst delivers an H2O2 production rate of 27.8 mol g−1 h−1 and a peak Faradaic efficiency of 91.7% at 150 mA cm−2. Mechanistic analyses combining electronic‐structure calculations and in situ vibrational spectroscopy reveal that sp hybridization reshapes frontier‐orbital distributions and local charge density, thereby coupling framework‐wide charge delocalization with favorable O2 adsorption and *OOH stabilization. These results establish bond hybridization as a molecular‐level design parameter for catalytic selectivity in COFs, extending framework engineering beyond conventional functional‐group and building‐block modification.
n727bf8b39f97: Chemical presodiation offers a promising pathway to compensate sodium deficiency in cathode and anode materials, thereby enhancing the usable energy density of sodium‐ion batteries. This approach is particularly critical for P2‐ and tunnel‐type cathodes, such as Na0.44MnO2, where the as‐synthesized materials typically exhibit a 50%–60% sodium deficiency. However, conventional presodiation reagents possess excessively high reductive potential, often leading to oversodiation, structural degradation, and compromised electrode reversibility. Here, we report a rational electron‐cloud engineering strategy to precisely control the sodium chemical potential of presodiation agents. Guided by Hückel's rule, we demonstrate that tailoring π‐conjugation size and introducing electron‐withdrawing groups enables the adjustment of sodium chemical potential via a balance of conjugative and inductive effects. We identify 1‐indanone as an optimal presodiation reagent, capable of delivering sodium to Na0.44MnO2 cathodes without any oversodiation. The resulting electrodes exhibit fully restored sodium inventories, an unprecedented first‐cycle Coulombic efficiency of ∼100%, and improved capacity retention over 350 cycles compared to untreated controls. Our findings establish a versatile framework for controlling sodium delivery in chemical presodiation, providing a new avenue for the design of next‐generation sodium‐ion batteries with enhanced stability and performance.
n2e3151f70e74: GPR15 (G Protein‐coupled Receptor 15), an atypical chemokine receptor, is implicated in the pathogenesis of multiple diseases, yet small‐molecule GPR15 antagonists remain undeveloped. Herein, we identify and characterize YL410, the first‐in‐class potent and selective GPR15 antagonist. In the cAMP‐GloSensor assay, YL410 inhibits GPR15 with an IC50 of 0.027 ± 0.005 µM, and displays high selectivity against a panel of related GPCRs and kinases. It suppresses GPR15L‐induced Jurkat T‐cell migration, and exhibits favorable pharmacokinetics and acceptable safety. Molecular docking, replicated molecular dynamics simulations, quantitative contact analyses, and mutagenesis experiments support a plausible orthosteric binding model for YL410, maintained by a reproducible network of polar and hydrophobic contacts, which rationalizes its potent antagonism and observed structure–activity relationships (SAR). Complementary AI‐based structure predictions (AlphaFold3, Chai‐1, and Boltz) recapitulated the energetically accessible orthosteric poses but not the dynamically stable pose selected by the MD simulations, underscoring the importance of kinetic‐stability validation in antagonist pose selection. Notably, in a diet‐induced obesity (DIO) mouse model, YL410 administration induced significant weight loss and exerted blood glucose‐lowering effects. Collectively, this study presents the first potent, selective, and in vivo efficacious GPR15 antagonist, providing new insights into the development of therapeutics for the treatment of obesity.
n12a7c6c63bd2: Reductive amination of aldehydes and ketones to primary amines is an important route for biomass valorization, yet achieving efficient synergy between substrate and hydrogen activation in cascade reactions remains challenging. Herein, we construct a compositionally tunable Ni─Al catalyst system whose architecture evolves from conventional Ni/Al2O3 to inverse Al2O3/Ni. This structural evolution gives rise to an unusual double-volcano catalytic behavior in furfural reductive amination. Two activity maxima are identified over 30Ni/Al2O3 and inverse Al2O3/90Ni, respectively, with the optimal Al2O3/90Ni catalyst delivering 98.5% furfurylamine yield and a space-time yield of 65 mmol gcat −1 h−1 under mild conditions. Adsorption studies, initial-rate kinetic isotope effect and reaction-order measurements, apparent activation-energy analysis, and in situ infrared spectroscopy indicate that the double-volcano behavior reflects the coupled evolution of catalyst composition and architecture and a composition-dependent balance between Lewis-acid-assisted intermediate formation and hydrogen-dependent intermediate conversion. Hydrogen-dependent steps exert a stronger kinetic influence over 30Ni/Al2O3 than over Al2O3/90Ni, while the inverse catalyst exhibits enhanced H2 adsorption and activation and more rapid Schiff base conversion. These results indicate a shift in the dominant kinetic limitation between the two catalysts and provide a framework for designing efficient non-noble-metal catalysts for multifunctional cascade reactions involving coupled substrate and hydrogen activation.
n4422e6412ac0: To address the limited piezocatalytic activity of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) arising from high structural symmetry and rapid charge recombination, an imine‐linked COFs (TFB‐TAPT) is synthesized by Schiff‐base condensation of 1,3,5‐triformylbenzene (TFB) and 2,4,6‐tri(4‐aminophenyl)‐1,3,5‐triazine (TAPT), followed by partial substitution of amino ligands with 1H,1H‐undecafluorohexylamine (UFHA) through a building‐block exchange strategy to afford TFB‐TAPT‐FA. This approach achieves controlled symmetry breaking with precise polar group distribution, without the lattice disruption caused by asymmetric monomers in one‐pot methods. The resulting randomly oriented polar nanoregions exhibit relaxation behavior, collectively generating a strong piezoelectric response under external stimuli. Piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM) measurements indicate that TFB‐TAPT‐FA has a piezoelectric coefficient of 140 pm/V, 2.5 times that of TFB‐TAPT. This amplification of the electromechanical response arises from the polar nanoregions, as evidenced by its higher calculated dipole moment (5.68 Debye). Consequently, TFB‐TAPT‐FA achieves an impressive piezocatalytic hydrogen production rate of 3.8 mmol g−1 h−1, marking a 17‐fold improvement over TFB‐TAPT. Notably, TFB‐TAPT‐FA enables efficient hydrogen production without cocatalysts or heterojunctions. More broadly, the introduction of polar nanoregions similarly enhances the performance of other imine‐linked COFs, demonstrating a potentially general strategy for designing piezocatalysts through nanoscale polarization engineering in COFs.
n3e8646b7dff4: Shuttle catalysis enables the transfer of reactive functional groups without relying on highly corrosive reagents. However, it remains largely confined to homogeneous systems, where catalyst recovery and reuse are often challenging. Here, we report a recyclable gold single‐atom catalyst (SAC) supported on activated carbon (AC) for the selective shuttle hydrochlorination of terminal alkynes to vinyl chlorides, which are key intermediates in pharmaceutical synthesis. Spectroscopic and catalytic studies indicate that the combination of Au(I) single atoms with the AC carrier is essential for the unique chemo‐ and stereoselectivity observed. This heterogeneous system displays broad substrate compatibility, including sterically hindered alkynes, heterocycles, acid‐labile groups, and drug‐derived substrates. Upon reuse, gradual aggregation of gold single atoms into nanoparticles leads to activity losses, but the associated speciation changes are reversible by oxidative redispersion, while quantitative metal retention ensures recoverability. Overall, this study demonstrates how to extend heterogeneous SACs to shuttle catalysis, highlighting the complementary reactivity and distinct catalyst design requirements for developing recoverable, safer, and more sustainable heterogeneous transfer reactions.
n76e78cf545f1: The efficient hydrogenation of CO2 to light olefins over Fe-based catalysts typically relies on the metal promoters, such as alkali or transition metals. In this study, we find that the intrinsic hydroxyl environments may be the crucial but long-overlooked factor governing the activity of Fe species. With the assistance of low-concentration guar gum, hydrogen-bond networks formed by dense hydroxyls are disrupted to generate isolated or terminal hydroxyl groups, which increase the active sites and significantly facilitate the product desorption. The resulting metal promoter-free Fe achieves a CO2 conversion of 30.1% and a light olefin selectivity of 38.1% at an ultra-high gas hourly space velocity of 300 000 mL gcat −1 h−1. Meanwhile, the space-time yield of light olefins reaches 3.3 kg kgcat −1 h−1, which outperforms all of the reported Fe-based catalysts modified by various promoters. These findings redefine hydroxyls as intrinsic promoters in Fe catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation and can potentially be extended to other heterogeneous catalytic systems and reactions.
n14369a705616: Precise regulation over the dimensionality and topology of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) through metal coordination remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, we report an in situ metal‐chelation strategy for topology regulation and single‐site construction in COFs using a bifunctional β‐hydroxy ketone‐functionalized HDBC monomer. Metal‐free Schiff‐base condensation of HDBC with TAPy affords a one‐dimensional covalent ribbon framework, named COF‐HDBC. Strikingly, in situ Cu2+ chelation during solvothermal crystallization redirects the assembly pathway toward a two‐dimensional bex‐type Cu‐COF‐HDBC containing framework‐embedded Cu─O coordination sites. Post‐synthetic metalation of preassembled COF‐HDBC fails to trigger this transformation, verifying the indispensable structure‐directing effect of in situ chelation during nucleation and growth. This strategy is extendable to Ni2+ and Co2+, affording isostructural metal‐chelated COFs. Multiscale characterizations and Cu K‐edge XAFS collectively support the proposed framework structures and the predominantly isolated nature of the Cu centers. As a functional validation, Cu‐COF‐HDBC enables selective CO2/CO electroreduction to CH4. This work establishes in situ metal chelation as a synthetic handle for programming COF topology and constructing framework‐embedded single‐metal sites, offering a versatile route to crystalline porous materials with complex architectures and tunable functions.
nfcc4e8ace503: Coupling electrochemical CO2 reduction showing high selectivity with microbial biosynthesis offering metabolic versatility offers a promising strategy for converting CO2 into value‐added products. We present proof‐of‐concept of electromicrobially producing the platform chemical itaconic acid (IA) from CO2 using a robust yeast chassis. The hybrid systems integrates in a single reactor electrochemical CO2 reduction with microbial synthesis using a synthetic autotrophic Komagataella phaffii strain. Thereby CO2 serves as carbon source while electrochemically generated formate from CO2 provides reducing power to sustain microbial growth and drive IA production, reaching average titres of 110.1 mg·L−1. While demonstrating the feasibility of directly coupling electrochemical and microbial processes within a single reactor, we reveal key challenges associated with integration, including limited system performance, variability in product titers, anodic oxidation of cathodic products, and constraints in energy efficiency. Despite these current limitations, our results establish the operational feasibility of integrated electromicrobial CO2 conversion using industrial yeast and highlight critical parameters for process intensification.
ncc79e8b17bd3: p-Type doping is an effective strategy for modulating molecular packing arrangement of organic compounds, thus improving their electrical conductivity. In this work, the first example of a mixed-valence radical cation dimer based on an odd alternant hydrocarbon, [OR5]2 +•[FeCl4]− (OR5-MV), was successfully prepared by the oxidation of olympicenyl radical (OR) derivative OR5 using FeCl3. X-ray crystallographic analysis revealed that cation-radical dimer [OR5]2 +•, acting as a fundamental building block, forms [OR5]4 2+ tetramer via a multi-center–two-electron bond, which further aggregates into a one-dimensional chain in the solid state. SQUID measurement reveals that the magnetic susceptibility is dominated by the FeCl4 – anions with no detectable OR5 moiety contribution. Theoretical calculations disclosed an open-shell singlet ground state for [OR5]4 2+ tetramer and demonstrated that the pancake-bond formation between OR5 cation-radical dimers confers significant energetic stabilization. Compared to the neutral compound, more uniform molecular packing and reduced intermolecular distance in the one-dimensional columnar architecture of OR5-MV facilitate effective intermolecular orbital overlap, leading to broader band dispersion along the molecular stacking direction. A substantially improved electrical conductivity of up to 10− 3 S cm− 1 is achieved compared to neutral radical (10− 9 S cm− 1), representing the highest value reported for monomeric odd alternant hydrocarbons.
n07777580afdf: The field of molecular photoswitches has grown tremendously over the past decades and pervaded every applied field from chemistry, biology, physics, to materials science and beyond. A main driver for continuous progress is tailoring absorption properties as a fundamental tool for controlling the light response. So far, the shift of absorption from UV light addressability into lower‐energy visible and red spectral regions has unlocked numerous unique opportunities, both in capability increase as well as in applicability of photoswitches. A next frontier has been opened more recently by extreme redshifting of absorption, allowing to enter the near‐infrared (NIR) spectral realm via direct excitation. This minireview highlights these important developments, delineates design principles to achieve NIR responsiveness in molecular photoswitches, and showcases the specific benefits that come with such low‐energy light control over molecular states. The outlook glimpses into the future and points out the particular opportunities and challenges ahead.
n9c04f195a7c8: Breaking the intrinsic adsorption conflicts among oxygen intermediates remains a central challenge in oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) electrocatalysis. Although spin‐state engineering offers an effective strategy for tuning catalytic activity, conventional approaches generally focus on a single‐spin configuration, which cannot simultaneously satisfy the distinct energetic requirements of different ORR intermediates. Here, we introduce an adaptive spin catalysis concept through proximity engineering of dual‐atomic Co sites confined within a one‐dimensional covalent organic framework. Precisely regulating the Co–Co separation while preserving the local coordination environment induces inter‐site electronic coupling, giving rise to coexisting high‐spin and low‐spin Co configurations. Combined spectroscopic characterizations and theoretical calculations support a mechanistic framework in which these coexisting spin configurations provide complementary catalytic functions for distinct intermediates along the multistep ORR pathway, thereby alleviating adsorption conflicts. Consequently, the proximity‐engineered catalyst delivers outstanding ORR activity with a half‐wave potential of 0.96 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode, outperforming both its spatially separated counterpart and commercial Pt/C. The catalyst also efficiently mediates both O2 and H2O2 reduction while suppressing peroxide decomposition, enabling enhanced performance in rechargeable zinc–air batteries and peroxide‐assisted aluminum–air batteries. This work establishes a molecular framework for exploiting spin‐state complementarity in atomic catalysts for advanced energy‐conversion reactions.
nd88cde2749f5: Hybrid organic-inorganic manganese halides have emerged as a promising class of emitters, owing to their excellent optical properties, low toxicity, and rich structural diversity. However, achieving site-specific control over their high-pressure optical response remains a great challenge. In this study, we report a zero-dimensional manganese chloride, (HIm)6[MnCl4∙MnCl6] (HIm = imidazolium), which concurrently incorporates both tetrahedral and octahedral Mn2 + centers within a single lattice. Under pressure, the red emission of [MnCl6]4− exhibits a pronounced and linear redshift and intensity attenuation. However, the green emission of [MnCl4]2− remains stable in both peak position and intensity, serving as a rigid energetic anchor. By leveraging the invariant green emission as an internal reference and the pressure-sensitive red emission as a probe, a self-calibrated pressure sensing system is achieved. Synchrotron high-pressure x-ray diffraction, in situ optical spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations demonstrate that this decoupled response originates from the large structural compressibility of the [MnCl6]4− octahedra and high rigidity of the [MnCl4]2− tetrahedra. Our findings demonstrate that hybrid organic-inorganic crystals represent a promising class of self-calibrated optical sensing materials for next-generation metrology.
n18475b3f44b5: Multiple resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) emitters with superior color purity and high photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) hold great promise for organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs). Nevertheless, the rigid planar structures and intrinsically slow reverse intersystem crossing rates (k RISC) of these materials lead to pronounced aggregation-caused quenching and significant efficiency roll-off. Here, we propose a sterically shielded heavy-atom strategy that simultaneously suppresses detrimental π–π stacking, accelerates k RISC, and reinforces the rigidity of the conjugated framework to retain narrowband emission. The proof-of-concept emitters BN-FLS, BN-FLSe, and BN-FLSSe show the green emission at 508–517 nm with the narrow full width at half maximums (FWHMs) of 25–26 nm in solution. Notably, BN-FLSSe achieves rapid k RISC of 4.2 × 106 s−1, maintains high PLQYs above 95%, and stable emission profiles over 1–30 wt% broad doping range. Non-sensitized OLEDs based on BN-FLS, BN-FLSe, and BN-FLSSe show pure-green electroluminescence with CIEy coordinates exceeding 0.70, high maximum external quantum efficiencies (EQEmaxs) of 41.7%, 41.1%, and 38.5%, and well-suppressed efficiency roll-offs, maintaining EQEs of 21.9%, 30.9%, and 32.7% at 1000 cd m−2, respectively. Impressively, even at high doping concentration of 30 wt%, these devices retain high EQEmaxs of 30.7%–33.1% with virtually unchanged emission spectra.
nc7d5197ad5a0: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) possess periodic skeletons and well-defined catalytic sites, allowing precise molecular-level regulation of interfacial properties in electrocatalytic oxygen reduction. However, conventional structural modifications fail to systematically tune oxygen adsorption geometry and interfacial electronic coupling. Here, we report a linkage-angle engineering strategy that alters the bonding positions of reactive aldehyde groups to fabricate three regioisomeric COFs with predefined backbone dihedral angles of 180°, 120°, and 60°. The angle‑driven regioisomeric effect induces considerable differences in dipole moments together with uneven charge distribution. These collective structural features remodel oxygen‑surface interactions and modulate the intrinsic catalytic kinetics. Theoretical calculations confirm that the compact 60° framework of o-TPDA-COF reconstructs confined pore interfacial microenvironments. Unlike the Griffiths‑type oxygen adsorption favored in its angular analogues, molecular oxygen preferentially adopts the Pauling configuration within o-TPDA-COF to stabilize OOH* intermediates. Consequently, the optimal o-TPDA-COF reaches an excellent H2O2 productivity of 12.82 mol gcat −1 h−1 and a Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 91.64%. This work realizes controllable modulation of oxygen‑adsorption behaviors in COF‑based 2e– oxygen reduction, delivering a novel geometry‑oriented design paradigm for porous electrocatalytic frameworks.
