nf8412247aa79: Single-atom alloys (SAAs) are an emerging class of heterogeneous catalysts that maximize atom efficiency by embedding isolated reactive metal atoms within a host metal surface, creating well-defined active sites. Atomic isolation imparts unique catalytic properties, including high selectivity, resistance to poisoning, coking, and sintering, and in some cases the ability to circumvent conventional scaling relationships that limit traditional catalysts. This article focuses on progress in the SAA field since our 2020 review (Chem. Rev.2020, 120, 12044−12088.), while incorporating earlier foundational studies where relevant. We first examine the fundamental principles governing SAA formation, stability, electronic structure, reactivity, and selectivity, drawing on insights from experimental single-crystal model systems and theoretical studies. We then review the application of SAAs in a wide range of industrially important reactions, including hydrogenation, dehydrogenation, selective oxidation, water–gas shift, Fischer–Tropsch synthesis, and dry reforming, among others. Beyond thermal catalysis, SAAs demonstrate great promise in electrocatalysis and plasmon-driven chemistry. Their structurally simple active sites have also enabled the rational design of novel catalysts and promoters that challenge conventional catalytic intuition. Looking ahead, recent advances in computing, including machine-learning potentials, offer the opportunity to explore vast compositional spaces and discover new alloy chemistries for challenging reactions using the SAA concept.
neaeb3c1505d4: Redox flow batteries (RFBs) have emerged as promising electrochemical energy storage technologies for long-duration stationary applications. Although aqueous RFBs represent the most commercially mature class, they are inherently limited by a narrow electrochemical stability window and high temperature sensitivity. Nonaqueous RFBs (NRFBs) expand the accessible voltage and temperature ranges, offering a promising route toward high-energy-density storage for long-duration and extreme-environment applications. However, their practical deployment remains impeded by several challenges, including high costs, insufficient power density, limited cycling stability, and safety concerns. This review offers a systematic synthesis of recent advances in key NRFB components, encompassing solvents, supporting electrolytes, membranes, electrodes, and redox-active molecules. We also highlight emerging methodologies expected to accelerate development, including machine-learning-enabled screening, advanced characterization, and life cycle assessment. Finally, this review compares aqueous and nonaqueous systems from commercialization and sustainability perspectives. Collectively, this review aims to advance design principles and optimization strategies for NRFBs, providing guidance for next-generation low-cost, high-energy-density flow battery technologies.

n6590c73a60cf: Prussian blue analogues AxM[Fe(CN)6]1–y·zH2O (A = Na, K, M = Fe, Mn) possess a rich crystal chemistry that allows their use as insertion materials for batteries, water treatment, and smart windows, among others, applications. Despite being simple in appearance, their synthesis is complex and often results in defective, nonstoichiometric materials. These defects can be of neutral charge, such as interstitial water molecules, or charged, such as A+ vacancies or [Fe(CN)6]n− vacancies, whose presence implies charge balance by the remaining transition metal centers. In this work, a compound close to the Berlin green Fe[Fe(CN)6] nominal composition was synthesized, and its crystal structure, electrochemical properties, and electronic structure were investigated. Although usual characterization methods such as X-ray diffraction, X-ray absorption spectroscopy, and 57Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy agree well with the formation of Fe[Fe(CN)6], the material can only be intercalated to Na1.4Fe[Fe(CN)6]. This lack of capacity was hypothesized to arise from “hidden” [Fe(CN)6] vacancies. The charge balance associated with these vacancies implies partial reduction of the low-spin Fe, as confirmed by low-temperature 57Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy and further high-angular-resolution diffraction experiments. This study suggests that numerous materials previously described as “Berlin green” in the literature might actually be substantially hexacyanoferrate defective.
nfecfae089ada: Area-selective atomic layer deposition (AS-ALD) fundamentally relies on a distinct disparity in surface chemical states between growth and nongrowth area. For SiO2/Cu patterned architectures, the oxidation of the Cu surface serves as a primary driver for the loss of selectivity as the ALD process proceeds. Herein, an alcohol-mediated AS-ALD process is proposed, utilizing alcohols with varying carbon chain lengths to precisely modulate surface chemical states to enhance selectivity of AS-ALD WOx film. A competitive-synergistic mechanism involving surface reductive capability and steric hindrance is identified as the governing factor for process selectivity. Results demonstrate that while the reducing ability of alcohols on oxidized Cu surfaces diminishes with increasing carbon chain length, their steric hindrance increases. EtOH was identified as the optimal pretreatment agent, yielding an exceptional selectivity exceeding 99.9% on SiO2/Cu patterned surface. Moreover, the alcohol-mediated AS-ALD process is successfully extended to other oxide systems with precursors bearing analogous ligands, demonstrating the generality of the proposed strategy. This work provides a versatile methodology for modulating surface reductive capability and steric hindrance to achieve high-selectivity AS-ALD.
n4b6cc05951ad: Colloidal germanium quantum dots (GeQDs) hold promise for solution-processable optoelectronics, yet their performance is often constrained by the limited reactivity of hydride-terminated surfaces and the insulating nature of conventional capping ligands. Here, we introduce a room-temperature selenylation strategy that harnesses the intrinsically weak and polarizable Ge–H bonds on freshly etched GeQD surfaces to drive Se–Se bond activation of diorganyl diselenides. This polarization-assisted concerted process proceeds without radical initiators or external stimuli, yielding robust Ge–SeR surface linkages that effectively passivate the GeQDs against oxidation while introducing a soft, polarizable chalcogenide-rich surface. The resulting RSe-GeQDs show notably improved optical properties and charge carrier mobilities compared to oleylamine-functionalized GeQDs. The direct, catalyst-free nature of this approach offers a versatile platform for the development of solution-processable germanium-based optoelectronic devices.
n9a6ea7e8b76f: Electrolytes composed of mixed solvents are of significant scientific and technological importance in lithium-ion and beyond-lithium-ion batteries, and more broadly across physical chemistry. Their emergence has highlighted the importance of multiscale phenomena, particularly the development of nanoscale solution heterogeneities. It is therefore essential to assess how these inhomogeneities and nanoscale aggregates influence solvation, transport, and electronic properties. Here we investigate the solution structure and transport properties of aqueous zinc sulfate electrolytes with acetonitrile (ACN) additives, where the addition of ACN leads to improved cyclability. Using complementary anomalous small-angle X-ray scattering, X-ray pair distribution function, electrochemistry, and NMR, we identify the presence of salt-rich-water-rich and salt-poor-ACN-rich nanoheterogeneities and, at higher ACN concentrations, liquid–liquid phase separation. We find that the size of zinc sulfate ion clusters in the water domains increases slightly upon ACN addition, while the ACN-rich domains grow much larger as phase separation is approached. The inverse Haven ratio, determined using the ionic conductivity and diffusivity, is much less than unity and decreases slightly upon addition of ACN, which shows ion–ion interactions. We speculate that the increased ion–ion interactions with increased ACN are a result of a reduction in free water, the increase in zinc sulfate cluster size, and/or an increase in solution tortuosity. This work highlights key phenomena to consider when engineering new water-organic-salt electrolyte systems and establishes a phase diagram for water–ACN–ZnSO4 that can guide advances, such as self-adaptive electrolytes.

n9bf97f69680b: Aviation's climate impact goes beyond CO2, yet current policies such as the EU's ReFuelEU regulation push almost exclusively toward sustainable fuels, overlooking an alternative: permanently capturing CO2 from the air via DACCS while continuing to burn fossil jet fuel. Comparing long-term costs of both approaches, we find DACCS is 49%–69% cheaper than synthetic fuels and needs far less renewable electricity, suggesting that current policy may be locking aviation into a costlier decarbonization path than necessary.
n24a7fb176953: Methane pyrolysis can produce hydrogen while sequestering solid carbon, but efficient high-grade heat delivery and coking management remain challenging. n4ba55fe3fe88: An oxide-modified copper phthalocyanine (CuPc) hole transport layer is proposed. The introduction of the Al 2 O 3 interlayer effectively suppresses interfacial carrier recombination.
n6afa807a96e1: Biowaste-derived multifunctional materials integrated with transition-metal oxides are emerging as sustainable photocatalysts owing to their tunable electronic properties, high catalytic activity, and environmental benignity. Herein, lignocellulosic pine-needle waste was valorized...
nd4c00d19279c: Deterministic spin–orbit torque (SOT) switching of perpendicular magnets without external magnetic fields remains a central challenge for scalable SOT-MRAM. Here, we demonstrate that dimensional engineering of a Co/W superlattice spin–orbit layer enables >90% field-free switching of perpendicular CoFeB. Harmonic Hall measurements reveal an unconventional out-of-plane torque, while first-principles calculations reveal reconstruction of the spin-resolved electronic structure and increased W-projected out-of-plane spin character, together supporting the modification of torque symmetry through Co/W superlattice engineering. The optimized superlattice achieves a critical current density of 23.3 MA cm–2 and a thermal stability factor Δ ≈ 45. Nanoscale devices (100 nm) preserve deterministic field-free reversal with comparable efficiency, confirming scalability toward magnetic tunnel junction integration. Micromagnetic analysis shows that out-of-plane spin-polarized torque together with canted anisotropy enables intrinsic symmetry breaking, highlighting superlattice engineering as a route to tailor torque symmetry for effective field-free SOT devices.
n12f10ed8fd85: Single-crystalline metals, with their distinctive symmetries, are the ideal medium for high-order molecular arrangement and the diminishing of grain boundaries and defect sites coupled with high anisotropy. However, conventional synthesis via bulk growth or epitaxial deposition remains complex, costly, and difficult to scale. Here, we report a simple and inexpensive strategy as an alternative to conventional strategies for manufacturing single-crystalline metal foils. Miraculously, by miniaturization of grain boundaries and promoting surface energy minimization during the rotation of the crystal lattice followed by the consumption of neighboring grains, high-quality and large-scale single-crystalline metal foils (Cu(111), Ni(111)) were obtained via vertically suspended chemical vapor deposition (CVD) annealing of polycrystalline metal foils. This discovery offers a potential strategy for manipulating and producing large-scale metal foils that may be used for industrial-scale applications.
n3fa7a23451ce: Electronic phases in quantum materials are often governed by nanoscale inhomogeneity, where local order develops within spatially confined regions, or puddles. A prominent example is an incommensurate charge-density-wave (I-CDW) comprising locally commensurate domains. In 2H-NbSe2, such an I-CDW state persists alongside lattice anharmonicity and superconductivity, raising fundamental questions about the dynamical stabilization of CDW order in puddles. Here, using Raman scattering, we reveal a strong Fano-coupling between interlayer shear phonons and the CDW amplitude mode. Our time-resolved reflectivity measurement shows a low-frequency ∼0.2 THz coherent overdamped oscillation onsetting within the CDW regime at ∼17K, indicating a previously unexplored transition. This we identify as a Fano-coupled phonon-CDW hybrid emerging from the collective dynamics of CDW puddles. We establish an overdamped-oscillator framework for capturing such intertwined glassy dynamics. These results highlight how lattice pinning and electronic correlations shape CDW order in layered materials, insight crucial for designing novel van der Waals devices.
n6eea938e73a1: Quantum dot light-emitting diodes (QD-LEDs) require encapsulation to extend their storage and operational lifetime. However, acidic encapsulants commonly used usually induce an anomalous positive aging phenomenon─the device performance improves rather than decreases in the initial days. These uncontrollable gains hinder the commercialization of QD-LEDs, yet no study to date has directly probed the in situ evolution of charge carriers during this process. Here, we employ electrically excited transient absorption (EETA) spectroscopy to investigate how encapsulants influence charge carrier dynamics in QD-LEDs. Taking red QD-LEDs as a model system, we demonstrate that positive aging is accompanied by enhanced electron charging in the quantum dot (QD) layer and accelerated electron injection into the emissive layer. Furthermore, we show that acid-induced progressive passivation of surface defects on ZnMgO nanoparticles improves electron injection efficiency. This work reveals that enhanced electron charging induces positive aging in QD-LEDs.
n5a254d60c0c3: Dual emissive materials are of particular importance in chemical and biological assays. Herein, we focus on a rod-shaped Au42(SCH2CH2Ph)32 nanocluster that exhibits dual emission at 875 and 1040 nm owing to fluorescence (FL) and phosphorescence (PH), respectively. Transient absorption analysis shows a slow intersystem crossing (ISC, ∼500 ps) from lowest singlet S1 to triplet T1 upon direct S1 excitation, leading to dual emission from both S1 and T1. However, upon excitation of the higher Sn state, we observe a metastable singlet state (S′). We rationalize two competing decay pathways from S′: (i) internal conversion to S1 and (ii) ISC to high triplet Tn≥2. These processes alter the populations of the S1 and T1 states, which explains the excitation-wavelength-dependent dual emission and FL/PH ratios. The revealed excited-state mechanism and the dual emissive Au42 material will serve as a paradigm for future research on atomically precise nanoclusters.
n866eeec6f551: Chemically and structurally diverse two-dimensional semiconductors exhibit a broad range of excitonic and optical phenomena that have direct implications for optoelectronic functionality. We examine these materials from a first-principles many-body perspective, emphasizing the connection between microscopic excitonic structure and optoelectronic functionality. Reduced symmetry and orbital character produce polarization-selective absorption, while dimensionality, dielectric screening, and exciton fine structure govern binding energies and radiative behavior. In layered systems, interlayer electrostatics and type-II band alignment promote charge separation, whereas exciton–phonon coupling activates indirect optical transitions and shapes temperature-dependent spectra. These mechanisms establish common design principles for excitonic engineering, whereby the dielectric environment, crystal geometry, lattice dynamics, and stacking are used to control exciton properties and tailor optical functionality. This perspective moves beyond description toward the ab initio prediction and design of emerging 2D materials for targeted optoelectronic applications, including polarization-sensitive photodetection and ultrathin solar-energy conversion.
n6c7461761eac: Fast-charging lithium-ion batteries require cathodes that sustain rapid Li+ transport while maintaining structural and interfacial stability. Here, we investigate particle-size effects in γ-MnO2 by comparing micron-sized (4.4 ± 0.8 μm) and nanosized (62 ± 21 nm) particles under identical conditions. Nanosized γ-MnO2 delivers 160.1 mAh g–1 at C/10 and retains ∼66% capacity at 5C while exhibiting lower charge-transfer and diffusion-related impedance. Cyclic voltammetry and Dunn’s analysis reveal a 68.9% capacitive contribution at 2 mV s–1, indicating a shift toward faster surface-controlled charge storage enabled by increased surface area and shorter Li+ diffusion pathways. GITT measurements show deeper lithiation (x ≈ 0.65 vs 0.48 in LixMnO2) and a more homogeneous solid-solution-like intercalation regime in nanosized particles, avoiding bulk phase-transition kinetic bottlenecks. The nanosized cathode retains 70% capacity with ∼99.5% Coulombic efficiency after 400 cycles at 3C, demonstrating particle-size engineering as an effective strategy for high-rate, long-life advanced battery energy storage.
n4a785d0868cf: The development of aqueous zinc batteries is critically constrained by the electrode–electrolyte interfacial instability at the Zn anode. Herein, a zwitterionic dynamic buffering interface (ZDBI) is constructed by using trace glufosinate ammonium (GA). The dissociated GA– anchors onto the Zn(101) surface via its phosphinate and carboxylate groups with its protonated amino group (−NH3+) extending into the electrolyte to dynamically respond to interfacial electric fields. Meanwhile, free NH4+ cations can form an electrostatic shielding layer under an electric field. This synergistic chemisorbed-mobile-ion buffering network thickens the electric double layer, inhibits water-splitting parasitic reactions, and induces (101)-oriented deposition. Consequently, Zn||Zn symmetric cells sustain stable cycling for over 7800 h with a cumulative capacity of 3.9 Ah cm–2, while Zn||Cu half-cells achieve an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.3%, and Zn||V2O5 full cells retain 88% capacity after 1000 cycles at 5 A g–1. This work offers an efficient strategy for addressing electrode–electrolyte interfacial issues.
n0fd77709f9e7: Emerging low-dimensional chiral perovskites have recently demonstrated significant application potential in circularly polarized light detection, spintronics, and quantum information technology due to their unique chiroptical activity and spin-selective properties. This review systematically summarizes their material systems, synthesis methods, chirality transfer mechanisms, and applications in photodetectors. The critical role of chiral organic cations in crystal regulation and chiroptical properties along with corresponding fabrication strategies is analyzed. Then, the inherent mechanisms of chirality transfer from organic to inorganic components are thoroughly discussed, encompassing structural distortion induction and electronic orbital coupling. Subsequently, recent advances in circularly polarized photodetectors based on low-dimensional chiral perovskites are highlighted from device performance, spin selection efficiency, to bio-inspired polarization vision systems. Finally, the challenges and future directions in this field are prospected. This review provides a comprehensive summarization for the development of low-dimensional chiral perovskites and their applications in next-generation polarized photodetectors.
nb960c4380d39: Hyperbolic media support high-k electromagnetic modes, enabling subdiffractional confinement, anomalous refraction, and enhanced light–matter interactions. While most hyperbolic metamaterials rely on artificial structuring, natural hyperbolicity arises from crystal anisotropy and direction-dependent plasma frequencies. Here we provide direct experimental evidence for natural hyperbolicity in copper chalcogenides by spectroscopic ellipsometry in the visible–near-infrared range. We demonstrate hyperbolic dispersion in bulk covellite CuS by identifying a spectral window where the real parts of the in-plane and out-of-plane permittivity components have opposite signs. The study is then expanded to size-controlled CuS nanosheets as oriented films. Using the Bruggeman effective medium approximation to account for the nanostructure/void composite, we show that hyperbolicity persists upon nanoscaling and that the epsilon-near-zero condition and hyperbolic bandwidth shift with size. Finally, we demonstrate analogous behavior in klockmannite CuSe nanosheets, establishing copper chalcogenides as a tunable platform for natural hyperbolicity at the boundary of the NIR and visible ranges.
n2fd16d2c42c9: Semiconductor hole spins offer a pathway to extended coherence times by decoupling from nuclear magnetic noise, while their spin–orbit coupling enables fast all-electrical control. In ZnSe, however, realizing this potential has been limited by p-doping challenges. Here, we circumvent this limit by optically activating acceptors and demonstrate optical spin initialization. We isolate a single-hole spin bound to a shallow acceptor, confirmed by antibunching and accessed via the fast (244 ps) radiative recombination of a bound exciton. Magnetic and Raman spectroscopy reveal a spin-selective Λ system with an effective hole g-factor of 0.7 and an optical line width of 26.7 GHz. Time-resolved measurements reveal optical pumping of the hole spin with an estimated initialization fidelity of 90.7%. First-principles simulations combined with the experiment identify nitrogen as the most likely acceptor impurity. These results introduce a promising new platform for optically active spin qubits and single-photon sources in ZnSe.
n1a1405fdf060: Aqueous zinc–iodine (Zn–I2) batteries are attractive for large-scale energy storage because of their low cost and inherent safety. However, the practical use of an I2 cathode is severely restricted by poor electronic conductivity and the shuttle effect of soluble polyiodides. Herein, a synergistic scaffold composed of MXene and carbon nanotubes (CNTs) modified with protonated polyaniline (PANI) via electrostatic interactions was designed. The MXene/CNT scaffold ensures overall conductivity and structural integrity. The protonated PANI immobilizes iodine species through nitrogen-containing groups and accelerates their interconversion, effectively suppressing the shuttle effect. The MXene/CNTs/PANI-I2 cathode with an iodine loading of 43.96 wt % achieves a superior specific capacity of 150 mAh g–1 at a high rate of 20 C as well as excellent cycling stability over 10 000 cycles. This work offers a viable strategy for developing stable I2 cathodes for high-performance Zn–I2 batteries.
nf91d5f2e13a5: HfO2/ZrO2-based (HZO) materials are promising high-k dielectrics for integrated capacitors and advanced electronic devices. However, their performance is fundamentally constrained by polymorph competition and the trade-off between the dielectric constant and leakage current. Here, we report a stacking-engineered strategy that integrates HZO layers with optimized ferroelectric and dielectric properties separated by an Al2O3 interlayer (HAZO). A nonswitching pulse measurement is employed to exclude polarization-switching contributions and directly probe the intrinsic dielectric response. The optimized HAZO dielectric exhibits an enhanced dielectric constant while simultaneously suppressing leakage and improving the dielectric breakdown characteristics. Structural characterizations reveal that the engineered stacking stabilizes the coexistence of nonpolar tetragonal and polar orthorhombic phases and increases the phase-boundary density. This polymorphic configuration suppresses irreversible domain switching and enables a stable enhanced dielectric response. These results establish a robust pathway toward high-performance HZO-based dielectrics and provide key insights into tailoring dielectric properties through polymorphic-phase engineering.
n71f3585b7a45: Efforts to improve carbon dioxide electroreduction have often focused on the catalyst. Now, by focusing on the gas instead, non-thermal plasma activation can unlock products that are not accessible through conventional electrocatalysis.
nf495575612b6: Integrating distinct weaving topologies within a single molecular network creates coupled deformation modes and adaptive adsorption behaviour, pointing to a shift from constructing molecular topologies to exploiting them for functions.
n860fed4f84de: Four-membered heterocycles are privileged scaffolds in medicinal chemistry, yet valuable thietanes remain underexplored compared with widely studied oxetanes and azetidines. Now a one-step skeletal editing strategy is reported that directly converts oxetanes into thietanes using thiourea.
n8cf20cf25776: Upon irradiation with visible light (λ = 425 nm), a tetrapeptide with a C-terminal photocatalytic site and an N-terminal site for substrate recognition promotes photochemical deracemization and enantioselective [2 + 2] photocycloaddition reactions. The required spatial proximity of catalyst and substrate is corroborated by NMR spectroscopy studies and molecular dynamics simulations.
neab46ce06322: Access to silylium ions with three different substituents has remained elusive owing to substituent scrambling under established synthetic methods. Now, harnessing the Lewis superacidity of halogen-substituted silylium ions, a broadly applicable protocol for synthesizing such heteroleptic silylium ions without substituent redistribution by halide abstraction from readily available halosilanes is reported.
n735725c0eb15: Ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) utilizing either a ferroelectric dielectric (FeD) or a ferroelectric semiconductor (FeS) are highly promising for neuromorphic computing. While integrating FeD with emerging FeS could provide new degrees of freedom for synaptic plasticity, direct integration inevitably suffers from unintended electrostatic coupling and a lack of independent polarization control. Here, we demonstrate a structurally decoupled dual-ferroelectric field-effect transistor (Dual-FeFET) based on an α-In2Se3/ZrO2/HZO heterostructure, in which a ferroelectric dielectric and a ferroelectric semiconductor are integrated into a single transistor while retaining independent functional roles. The inserted ZrO2 interfacial layer mitigates unintended polarization coupling between HZO and α-In2Se3, enabling two orthogonal memory operations: gate-bias-induced HZO polarization switching globally modulates the carrier density of the α-In2Se3 channel, whereas drain-bias-induced α-In2Se3 polarization switching predominantly modulates the drain-side Schottky barrier near the contact region. Dual-mode PFM, Hall-bar analysis, temperature-dependent transport measurements, and ZrO2-thickness-dependent control experiments support the largely decoupled modulation of channel transport and contact injection. By sequentially exploiting these two modulation modes, the Dual-FeFET extends the conductance dynamic range and improves the linearity of synaptic potentiation compared with conventional single-mode FeFET operation. The device exhibits robust nonvolatile memory characteristics with stable endurance over 105 cycles and retention up to 105 s. When implemented in convolutional neural network simulations for CIFAR-10 image recognition, the Dual-FeFET-based synapses achieve an accuracy of 89.2%, approaching the ideal software accuracy of 96.5% and outperforming conventional single-FeFET-based synapses (74.1%). These results demonstrate that structural ferroelectric decoupling enables independently programmable channel and contact modulation in multifunctional 2D ferroelectric transistors.
n828307d5b742: Effective transdermal drug delivery (TDD) demands both the ability to bypass the stratum corneum (ST) and the robustness to sustain delivery efficiency under real-life conditions. Despite advances in nanocarriers, microneedles, and electrostimulation, many TDDS strategies face limitations due to cytotoxicity, invasiveness, device dependence, and poor performance for large molecules in real-world conditions. In this study, we present a marine-inspired TDDS patch (PDA@SC) that integrates adhesion strategies from marine organisms to achieve stable skin attachment and atraumatic macromolecular delivery, even on dynamic skin surfaces. The suction-cup (SC) structure, inspired by octopus’ suckers, generates negative pressure upon preload-induced deformation, promoting temporary mechanical modulation for nanolevel control of the ST barrier and enhancing drug delivery without external power. Simultaneously, the mussel-inspired polydopamine (PDA) coating modifies hydrophobic surfaces into high surface energy interfaces capable of chemical bonding, thereby ensuring intimate adhesion and minimizing drug leakage. Experimental findings confirmed that the delivery of the high molecular weight compound was enhanced on deformed skin, showing a 600% improvement compared to conventional topical application. In addition, preliminary human evaluation demonstrated that PDA@SC effectively improved key dermatological parameters. Collectively, these results highlight the potential of PDA@SC as a platform that can drive technological progress in wearable therapeutics and cosmetics.
n02dac954595f: Ovarian cancer, the most lethal gynecologic malignancy, urgently demands early and accurate diagnostic methods. Tumor-derived extracellular vesicles (tEVs) hold great promise as noninvasive biomarkers, yet their clinical translation is severely hampered by inherent heterogeneity and the inability of conventional assays to detect multiple types of biomarkers. To break this bottleneck, we developed a novel one-pot, triple-encoding platform that integrates size–fluorescence-encoded beads with a membrane fusion strategy. This enables simultaneous in situ profiling of 11 miRNAs across three distinct EV subpopulations defined by EpCAM/PD-L1 expression. Leveraging machine learning, an 11-miRNA logistic panel achieved tumor versus health discrimination (AUC = 0.995), and a combinatorial signature based on EV subpopulations and miRNA profiles enabled the classification of ovarian cancer subtypes, achieving 78.6% accuracy in the validation cohort. Our work provides a versatile and scalable approach for multiparameter EV analysis, enabling comprehensive EV miRNA profiling and ovarian cancer classification.
n878cdac60aef: Posttranslational sulfur incorporation into peptide backbones is increasingly reported. These efforts broaden our understanding of thioamides, which have distinct conformational and hydrogen‐bonding properties compared with amides. YcaO‐catalyzed thioamidation of the ribosomal protein uL16 reportedly occurs across thousands of Pseudomonadota. Here, we identify the cysteine desulfurase IscS, a crucial component of iron–sulfur cluster assembly, as the direct sulfur donor for uL16 thioamidation. Genetic deletion, in vitro reconstitution, kinetic analysis, sulfide scavenging, and mutational studies support this conclusion. Our data support a mechanism in which the IscS persulfide attacks the O‐phosphorylated uL16 backbone amide to form an IscS–uL16 disulfide intermediate. This labile disulfide is rapidly reduced, and the resulting hemiorthothioamide collapses with phosphate release to give the thioamide. IscS binds uL16 with mid‐nanomolar affinity and can be displaced by other IscS‐dependent sulfur acceptors. IscS promotes formation of the 2:2 YcaO–uL16 complex from the otherwise predominant 1:1 complex. Structural and mutational studies identify uL16 residues important for catalytically competent enzyme–substrate interactions. These findings define the sulfur delivery pathway for uL16 thioamidation and reveal an additional role of the IscS persulfide beyond iron–sulfur cluster assembly, suggesting it serves as another nucleophile for YcaO‐catalyzed backbone modification.
n6ce9576b7864: While the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of organic solar cells (OSCs) has advanced rapidly, their sensitivity with respect to active layer thickness hinders industrial fabrication. Herein, a novel acceptor BMD‐6F was synthesized via molecular engineering of L8‐BO, which realizes synergistic optimization of dielectric constant (6.20, 1.5 × that of L8‐BO) and H‐aggregation and thus enriches charge transport pathways, facilitates exciton dissociation, and suppresses recombination. As a result, the PM6:L8‐BO:BMD‐6F ternary OSC delivered a champion PCE of 20.34% at 100 nm, and exhibited excellent thickness tolerance with PCEs of 18.23% (300 nm) and 16.18% (500 nm). This work establishes a design principle for high‐efficiency, thickness‐tolerant OSCs, promising industrial applications.
n3a0704437377: The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains a major kinetic bottleneck in anodic water splitting because of sluggish adsorption and desorption kinetics of O-containing intermediates. Optimizing the adsorption strength of various O-containing intermediates in accordance with the Sabatier principle involves the precise tuning of the active-site electronic structure. Herein, we explore a p-block metal-assisted synergism regulation strategy in NiFe layered double hydroxides (LDHs) by introducing group-13 elements (Al, Ga, In) as dopants. Among various doped LDHs, In-doped NiFe-LDH shows the highest OER activity by demanding an overpotential value of 298 mV at 10 mA/cm2 along with enhanced intrinsic turnover frequency and long-term stability. X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) reveals that In3+ preferentially occupies the Fe coordination sites, while valence-band X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (VB-XPS) confirms enhanced electronic coupling in the Ni–O–In framework. Density functional theory (DFT) additionally suggests that the In 5p orbitals strongly hybridize with the O 2p and Ni 3d states, establishing a Ni3d-O2p-In5p electronic interaction that regulates the Ni electronic structure and optimizes the adsorption energies of O-containing intermediates. The resulting d-p-p orbital hybridization offers an efficient pathway for charge delocalization and strengthens the M–O covalency, thereby accelerating the OER kinetics. This study elucidates the structure–activity relationship and identifies p-block metal-induced orbital hybridization as an effective strategy for developing high-performance oxygen evolution electrocatalysts, offering an alternative to conventional transition-metal modification approaches.
n0d483db6fb87: Understanding the correlated dynamics of multiple molecular rotators in crystalline supramolecular assemblies is essential for designing functional molecular machines, yet deconvoluting the motions of distinct components remains inherently challenging due to the limitations of individual techniques. Here, we report a synergistic approach that combines solid-state Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (SSNMR) and dielectric spectroscopy to quantitatively resolve multirotor dynamics in a family of isostructural supramolecular gyroscopic complex architectures composed of alkyl ammonium, crown ether, and metal halide hydrate. SSNMR unambiguously reveals both the tert-butylammonium cation and the 18-crown-6 macrocycle as independent rotators─a distinction often ambiguous in such systems. Crucially, by correlating SSNMR-derived dynamics of the crown ether with dielectric relaxation of the coordinated water molecule, we uncover their synchronized rotation across a wide temperature range, mediated by charge-assisted hydrogen bonding. These findings reveal a cooperative multirotor gyroscopic model featuring synchronous rotation of an integrated coaxial crown ether–water–ammonium trio-rotator, accompanied by correlated alkyl reorientation. This synergy validates the dielectric relaxation principle in a complex, multirotor crystalline environment where unambiguous peak assignment has been a longstanding challenge. This work establishes a generalizable methodology for dissecting complex, multicomponent dynamics in crystalline materials, directly bridging molecular-scale motion to macroscopic dielectric response.
n815edb2d6801: Phosphorus-mediated reactions that leverage the thermodynamic driving force of phosphorus(III) oxidation are crucial in all areas of the chemical industry. While substantial progress has been made in phosphorus(III/V) redox organocatalysis to develop catalytic alternatives, the rising field of redox-neutral phosphorus(V) organocatalysis has revealed new modes of phosphorus-based reactivity in chemical transformations without requiring stoichiometric reductants. This review highlights key advances in redox-neutral phosphorus(V) organocatalysis with a focus on fundamental phosphorus(V) reactivity, organized by the catalyst structure and emphasizing its role as a Lewis acid, Brønsted acid/base, nucleophile, superbase, or single-electron transfer agent. We close with remarks connecting established reactivity paradigms that will likely be applied to new generations of phosphorus(V) catalysts capable of solving modern synthetic challenges.
nba601eabbaba: Metal promotion is a widely adopted strategy to enhance the activity of indium oxide (In2O3) catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol. However, intimately contacted metal promoters on In2O3 often result in rapid catalyst deactivation, as excessive local H2 supply induces undesirable structural degradation of the In2O3 domain. Here, we address this limitation by implementing a carbon nanotube (CNT)-mediated hydrogen transport pathway, which spatially separates the H2 activation sites (Pd) from the CO2 hydrogenation sites (In2O3) at the catalyst preparation stage. Intriguingly, upon reductive activation, the initially separated components spontaneously evolve into a distinctive interfacial configuration. In this configuration, InOx migrates onto and partially covers the Pd nanoparticles, forming an InOx@Pd inverse interface. Unlike the directly constructed Pd–In2O3 interface, which suffers from over-reduction to metallic In0 accompanied by sintering and alloying with Pd, this CNT-derived interface preserves the In3+ oxidation state and serves as a non-destructive junction for hydrogen delivery. Combined with long-range hydrogen spillover across the CNT network, this architecture transforms a concentrated and destructive hydrogen flux into a regulated supply that reaches distal In2O3 domains without driving over-reduction. Consequently, the Pd/CNT + In2O3 system exhibits both improved catalytic activity and enhanced long-term stability (>230 h), whereas the conventional Pd/In2O3 catalyst deactivates continuously. These findings demonstrate that a controlled hydrogen delivery system between H2 activation sites and active sites on the oxide domain offers an effective way for developing active and durable catalysts involving reduction-sensitive oxide phases.
n6f11caf20cab: Electric field-enhanced electrocatalysis represents an innovative strategy for improving the efficiency of electrochemical transformations. However, quantitative evaluation of microscopic electric-field effects under operando conditions remains challenging, limiting a rigorous, predictive understanding of field-mediated reaction regulation. Here, by integrating rigorous numerical methods, constant-potential microkinetic simulations, and machine learning models, we establish electric-field intensity as a quantitative descriptor that directly correlates local fields with catalytic performance. Using curvature-engineered M–N–C single-atom catalysts as a model platform, we demonstrate that curvature-induced electric fields modulate electron occupation at active sites and shift the potential of zero charge in a controllable manner. This field-driven electronic perturbation selectively tunes adsorbate binding energetics, thereby dictating limiting potentials, steering reaction pathways, and governing the thermodynamics and kinetics of interfacial proton-coupled electron transfer in nitrogen electroreduction. Notably, we uncover an inverted volcano–type dependence of catalytic activity on curvature, wherein optimal activity is achieved within a moderate field-strength window. This nonmonotonic trend underscores the necessity of balanced curvature regulation, rather than simply maximizing field intensity, in optimizing electrocatalytic performance. These findings provide a quantitative framework for monitoring and regulating catalytic trends under realistic operating conditions via curvature-induced electric fields, offering generalizable design principles for diverse SAC systems and electrochemical reactions.
nf961ffd71938: Achieving a high propane conversion in propane dehydrogenation to propylene (PDH) carries tremendous scientific and economic value, particularly if achievable with established industrial units. Here we propose a diffusion-selective modulation strategy driven by large-scale machine-learning computation, where the key to success lies in finding auxiliary materials to drive the PDH reaction forward by enlarging the diffusion-rate difference between H2 and C3 species. This strategy is demonstrated theoretically via high-throughput computation and then validated experimentally through the introduction of inert siliceous CHA zeolites as a diffusion-selective modulator within the catalyst bed. By simply physically mixing CHA with various PDH catalysts, we show that the single-pass propane conversion can increase by 1–5% from industrial space velocities (10 h–1) to significantly higher throughputs (256 h–1), consistently improving performance across multiple reported catalysts without compromising stability. This “plug-and-play” methodology can be directly implemented in existing industrial PDH units without altering either the catalyst formulation or the reactor configuration, providing a readily implementable and scalable route for upgrading current PDH infrastructure.
n39175cb0e5a6: Metallo-β-lactamases (MBLs) are key contributors to antimicrobial resistance (AMR). The L1 MBL, originally from Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, is a tetrameric, dizinc, subclass B3 MBL that efficiently hydrolyzes most β-lactam antibiotics and evades inhibitors that act on other MBLs. Using quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (DFTB3/MM) simulations with enhanced sampling, we mapped the full reaction pathway and minimum free energy profile for L1-catalyzed hydrolysis of faropenem, a penem antibiotic whose reaction can yield alternative enamine and imine products. Benchmarking against B3LYP-D3/6-31G(d) shows that DFTB3 provides the best correlation between energy and structure for this system. We test different possible mechanisms and find that changes in hydration at the metal site during the catalytic cycle are critical for efficient hydrolysis. Our results show that a zinc-bridging hydroxide acts as the nucleophile, with the conserved active site residue D120 participating in back-and-forth proton-transfer events and stabilizing the enzyme-intermediate (EI) complex. The direct reaction of EI, however, involves a large energy barrier; the second stage is facilitated by diffusion of a water molecule into the active site. This water molecule was observed during long-timescale MM MD simulations using the Extended Zinc Amber Force Field (EZAFF). Direct proton transfer from this water to the substrate amide nitrogen forms an enamine product, while imine formation requires rotation of the faropenem 6α-hydroxyethyl substituent to enable proton transfer from water to the substrate C2. The calculated free energy barriers for the formation of both products are consistent with the experimentally determined catalytic constant, and the calculated greater stability of the imine with its crystallographic observation. These simulations provide dynamic insight into L1 catalysis, highlighting features that can be exploited for inhibitor design.
n750648f5ba39: Thiophenes are readily available sulfur heteroarenes and prominent motifs in medicinal and synthetic chemistry, but their direct heterogeneous hydrogenation to thiolanes remains challenging due to sulfur-induced catalyst deactivation and competing hydrodesulfurization. Here, we report a chloroform-induced surface modification strategy that enables the heterogeneous Pd(OH)2/C-catalyzed hydrogenation of thiophenes to saturated sulfur heterocycles. The method proceeds under mild hydrogenation conditions and provides access to a range of alkyl-, silyl-, aryl-, and benzofused thiolane derivatives. A hydrogenation-focused robustness assessment revealed compatibility with several functional groups that are commonly sensitive under Pd/H2 conditions, while preparative scope studies showed that functional-group-containing thiophenes can be converted when potentially interfering motifs are separated from the thiophene core by suitable alkyl or aryl spacers. Mechanistic experiments indicate that CHCl3 is not merely a beneficial solvent: CHCl3/H2 pretreatment of Pd(OH)2/C generates a catalytically competent material whose activity is retained after replacing CHCl3 with 2-MeTHF. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (ToF-SIMS) analyses support the formation of persistent chloroform-derived organochlorine/C–Cl-type surface environments and chlorocarbon fragments. These findings establish solvent-induced catalyst modification as a useful design principle for challenging heterogeneous hydrogenations of sulfur-containing heteroarenes.
na500abd96e0f: Formamidinium lead iodide (FAPbI3) perovskites are promising for high-performance solar cells; however, the low surface energy of self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) impedes α-phase nucleation in inverted devices. Here, we report a formamidinium (FA)-solvent intermediate-mediated self-seeding crystallization strategy to enable quality α-phase FAPbI3. By employing N-formylmorpholine (NFM) as a non-toxic solvent, (FA···NFM)PbI3 intermediates are formed, thereby lowering the phase-transition barrier and promoting the spontaneous formation of α-phase nuclei at the early stage of crystallization. These preformed nuclei serve as intrinsic seeds, facilitating rapid nucleation and orientated crystal growth. Consequently, NFM-based devices achieve efficiencies of 26.41% and 26.56% using 2-methoxyethanol (2-Me) and N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) as primary solvents, respectively, with a 1 cm2 device reaching 25.47%. The unencapsulated devices retain 85% and 90% of their initial efficiencies after 1200 h illumination and 1400 h thermal aging at 85 °C, respectively.
n63eaef75d86b: Silicon anodes unlock higher energy density in Li-ion batteries but suffer from poor calendar life due to inadequately passivating solid–electrolyte interphases (SEIs). Here, we contrast the calendar aging behaviors of single- and mixed-salt locally superconcentrated electrolytes (LSCEs) against carbonate electrolytes. Mixed-salt LSCE cells retained 96% and 44% of precalendar capacity after one month and then after five months, while carbonate electrolyte cells retained 77% and 1%, respectively. The mixed-salt LSCE advantage is tied to the formation of a predominantly inorganic SEI, evidenced by nanoscale Fourier transform infrared spectromicroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and 3D time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry. After 5 months, however, perturbations to SEIs were evident in all cells, accelerating voltage decay and capacity loss by lithium inventory loss associated with SEI growth. These findings suggest that future electrolytes may benefit from strategies that continuously reinforce the SEI through controlled anion and solvent redox in LSCEs.
nc27262397bb8: Inefficient immune synapse formation limits the therapeutic efficacy of T cell-based immunotherapy in both solid tumors and hematological malignancies. Here, we report a fully synthetic, membrane-anchored dual-targeting aptamer engager, AptE 2, that acts as a programmable artificial immunological interface to redirect cytotoxic T cells toward cancer cells without genetic engineering. Constructed entirely from DNA aptamers through optimized bioorthogonal conjugation and enzyme-mediated ligation, AptE 2 integrates multivalent tumor recognition, T cell binding, enhanced nuclease resistance, and prolonged membrane anchoring within a single modular scaffold. In colorectal cancer models, AptE 2 promoted stable T cell–tumor cell engagement, enhanced cytotoxicity and cytokine secretion, and drove pronounced tumor regression with increased intratumoral CD8+ T cell infiltration and minimal systemic toxicity. Importantly, AptE 2 also demonstrated broad applicability in leukemia. In CCRF-CEM cells, AptE 2 exhibited strong surface binding, sustained membrane retention for up to 6 h, and superior resistance to wash-off compared with monovalent aptamers and bivalent controls. AptE 2-prearmed TALL-104 cells markedly enhanced leukemia cell clustering, increased cell lysis to over 90% under optimized coculture conditions, and amplified IFN-γ secretion. In a disseminated CCRF-CEM-Luc leukemia mouse model, AptE 2-mediated T cell therapy suppressed systemic leukemia progression, improved peripheral hematological profiles, and showed favorable tolerability without detectable major organ injury. These findings establish AptE 2 as a generalizable, nonprotein-based and nonviral immune engager platform for programmable T cell redirection across both solid and hematological cancers.
naac43e0c5160: The Golgi apparatus (GA) has emerged as a promising target for cancer therapy. Commonly, therapeutics are guided to the GA by recognizing specific receptors on the GA membrane. Consequently, the transfected cells exhibited GA structural disassembly and underwent a pyroptosis-like programmed cell death with immunogenic characteristics. Notably, αHL-rich microvesicles were subsequently secreted, effectively killing neighboring tumor cells. Furthermore, by incorporating iRGD-modified polymers, we constructed a tumor-targeting oncolytic virus-like nanoparticle with neutral surface charge. Following intravenous administration, this iRGD-modified nanoparticle could efficiently suppress tumor growth without causing obvious systemic toxicity. Collectively, this work presents a robust strategy for GA-targeting via sphingomyelin recognition, providing a potential approach for GA-targeted anticancer therapeutics.
n7bfd6f158d6b: The global prevalence of Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection stands in stark contrast to the limited clinical efficacy of antibiotics, primarily attributed to their rapid inactivation under gastric acidity and poor penetration through the gastric mucus barrier. This platform is constructed from poly(amino acid) block copolymers (FAR) incorporating d-aminoalanine side chains and rhamnolipid (RHL) moieties, which self-assemble into amoxicillin-loaded nanoparticles (Am@FAR NPs). Under strongly acidic gastric conditions (pH < 3), Am@FAR NPs undergo extensive protonation, adopting a compact, stabilized configuration that suppresses premature drug release and preserves antibiotic activity. Upon entering the gastric mucus layer (pH ∼ 4–6), partial deprotonation induces surface charge reversal, reducing nonspecific mucin adhesion and facilitating efficient mucus penetration. Cooperative recognition, mediated by RHL and d-aminoalanine residues, enables selective targeting of H. pylori within the mucus niche; here, further local pH elevation (∼6–7) triggers particle swelling and on-site drug release. Consequently, Am@FAR NPs achieve 99.99% eradication efficiency against H. pyloriin vivo, offering a highly effective and biocompatible strategy for the treatment of gastric H. pylori infections.

nafe452ce86d0: Operando nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy provides unique insight into chemical changes in batteries during use but has largely been limited to custom plastic cells. Unfortunately, the metal casings that house commercial batteries distort and shield radiofrequency (RF) fields required for excitation and detection in NMR. Here, we use operando7Li NMR spectroscopy to study metal-encased batteries in both coin and pouch cell formats without modifying the cell or casing. We benchmark NMR spectra obtained from stainless-steel coin cells and aluminum-laminate pouch cells to plastic coin cells and show that casing composition, auxiliary hardware, and sample placement strongly influence observed shift, signal intensity, and line shape due to bulk magnetic susceptibility effects and RF attenuation upon interacting with cell parts. These effects are most severe in stainless-steel coin cells (and in particular 304-grade stainless steel) but can be mitigated through the use of Al spacers while retaining the stainless-steel caps and springs. In light of these considerations, we leverage operando7Li NMR to track lithium plating/stripping and monitor the accumulation of electrochemically inactive “dead” lithium (Li0) during galvanostatic cycling in coin and pouch cells. In pouch cells, the lean electrolyte volume allows us to resolve changes in the 7Li electrolyte signal during formation that are consistent with electrolyte redistribution and wetting. Taken together, these results demonstrate how to alter cell susceptibility to improve NMR signals during operando measurements in commercially relevant form factors while also establishing the cell design constraints that limit quantitative interpretation.
nad30fd7589e8: Most zero-dimensional hybrid metal halides enable emission in the first near-infrared (NIR-I) region (650–950 nm), and the shorter wavelengths result in poor photon penetration depth. Although a variety of mechanisms are involved in the explanation of such a broad band with a large Stokes shift, the exploration of the structural origin of the NIR optical activity remains challenging due to misconceptions about excitons and experimental limitations. A family of hybrid metal halides doped with Bi3+,In3+ or Bi3+/In3+ demonstrates that the fine interplay between the Jahn–Teller effect and spin–orbit coupling (SOC) takes into full consideration orbital degeneracy and electron flipping, thus boosting the photoluminescence quantum yield to 12%. TD-DFT calculations visualize the symmetry of the two lattices within a dimeric structure varying with specific modes, and the rational assignment of the energy gap (ground state: 3.69 eV; excited state: 1.22 eV) between 1S0 and 3P1 is highly consistent with the experimental findings (λex = 330 nm; λem = 1100 nm). Leveraging the (BTBAC)2Sb2Cl8 sample, electroluminescence pumped by a UV-LED chip yields a highly efficient NIR-II emission, and the phosphor displays diverse functions in night vision and anticounterfeiting.
n3669aa92aec2: We present monoclinic strontium manganese oxide as a bifunctional electrocatalyst for Zn–air batteries. Moreover, in situ XAS was used to investigate the oxidation states and local structures of strontium and manganese ions during the ORR and OER.
naf6454ea1778: Constructing efficient heterojunctions for overall CO 2 photoreduction remains challenging due to the difficulty in achieving intimate interfacial contact and directional charge transfer between components. Herein, we report a semiconductor-induced Z-scheme...
nf0abb4fc2066: Large magnetoresistance typically emerges from transitions between distinct electronic phases or magnetic configurations, yet controllable switching between competing magnetic configurations within a single metallic material remains challenging. Here we investigate magnetotransport in Cr3Te4 and demonstrate a magnetic-field-switchable resistance modulation of up to −37.6%, enabled by the near degeneracy between antiparallel and parallel magnetic configurations. Remarkably, a magnetic field of ∼0.25 T suffices to induce switching between these competing magnetic configurations, accompanied by a reconstruction in electronic transport supported by Boltzmann transport calculations. Substituting 5% of Cr with Co suppresses the switching behavior, consistent with a suppression of the competition between the nearly degenerate magnetic configurations, while the magnetoresistance evolves into a negative longitudinal magnetoresistance, suggesting a possible Weyl-band-related contribution associated with a Co-induced upward shift of the Fermi level. Our results establish competing magnetic configurations as an effective route toward large magnetoresistance in structurally simple metallic systems.
n536ee83b8945: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is attractive for multiplex bioimaging owing to its excellent photostability and ultranarrow spectral bandwidth. However, achieving synergistic enhancement of excitation and Raman scattering fields remains challenging. Herein, the relationship between geometry and localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) was investigated by continuously tuning the aspect ratio (AR) of anisotropic Au nanopolyhedrons (Au NPHs). Central-body modulation while preserving sharp terminal tips enables continuous LSPR tuning while retaining tip-associated electromagnetic enhancement. The SERS behavior was further analyzed by considering the spectral matching between the LSPR and the excitation/scattering wavelengths. For different excitation wavelengths, the optimal SERS response can be achieved by selecting Au NPHs whose LSPR band best matches with the excitation and Raman scattering wavelengths. These results demonstrate that Raman enhancement is governed by spectral matching rather than a fixed optimal geometry. The optimized Au NPHs enabled the use of dual SERS probes for proof-of-concept multiplex biomarker imaging.
n8eef202e8fa3: Transient states of matter far from equilibrium may exhibit physical properties beyond those allowed by the equilibrium-state crystalline symmetries. We explore ultrafast and direct electronic excitations of transient states in a dirty-limit superconductor with time-resolved terahertz-pump terahertz-probe spectroscopy. By embedding the superconductor into a designed microcavity structure of metallic split-ring resonators, we can sensitively probe the pump field-induced transient variations of the superconducting states around the cavity’s resonant frequency. Our results show that the strong terahertz field can transiently modify the symmetries of the electronic subsystems via the injection of a picosecond supercurrent, leading to high-order nonlinear dynamical responses that are not compatible with the equilibrium-state symmetries, which is evidence for transient symmetry breaking on the picosecond time scale.
n9064a7485c6d: Probing the internal electronic structure of complex materials with atomic spatial resolution has remained an outstanding challenge in condensed-matter science. A promising approach is convergent-beam electron diffraction (CBED) in four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM). Here, we apply 4D-STEM CBED to the charge-density-wave (CDW) material 1T-TaS2. We demonstrate a qualitative breakdown of the conventional independent atom model (IAM) in reproducing the experimental CBED patterns. A robust low-angle intensity maximum is systematically absent in IAM-based simulations but is consistently reproduced in simulations that use electrostatic potentials derived from density functional theory. A comparison of CBED patterns with projected charge densities reveals a remarkable correspondence between the local real-space valence charge distribution and diffracted intensities, reflecting site-dependent charge density variations within the CDW structure. These results establish atomic-resolution CBED as an experimental probe of valence electron contributions to the scattering potential and open a route to resolving complex electronic ordering phenomena.
n3656e45e1d9e: Electronic metal-support interactions (EMSI) provide an effective means of tuning the electronic structure of supported metal catalysts and thereby modulating their catalytic properties. However, how the crystal phase of supports governs EMSI and in turn influences the selective hydrogenation remains largely unexplored. Here, we report a crystal-phase engineering strategy to precisely regulate EMSI in ultrafine Ir nanoclusters (NCs) supported on polymorphic Nb2O5. Comprehensive spectroscopic characterization reveals that the orthorhombic Nb2O5-T phase forms a distinctive socketed metal-support interface that strongly anchors Ir NCs and induces substantial electron transfer from the support to the metal. Distinct from classical strong metal-support interactions that often compromise active-site accessibility, this socketed interfacial configuration simultaneously enhances EMSI, stabilizes the Ir NCs, and preserves abundant exposed active sites. The resulting electron-rich Ir species facilitates H2 activation and interfacial hydrogen spillover while favoring preferential adsorption of the carbonyl group over the C=C bond in α, β-unsaturated aldehydes. Consequently, Ir@Nb2O5-T exhibits high activity, selectivity, and durability for the selective hydrogenation to unsaturated alcohols under mild conditions, overcoming the typical activity–selectivity trade-off. This work establishes a direct crystal phase–EMSI–reactivity relationship and highlights crystal-phase engineering as a powerful strategy for manipulating metal–support interfaces toward highly selective heterogeneous catalysis.
n4ff36b0ff4c7: Inverse Ga2O3-Pt catalysts have exhibited better catalytic performance in propane dehydrogenation due to their tunable interfacial electronic properties. This study explores the potential of inverse Ga2O3-Pt catalysts and their single-atom-doped variant (Ga2O3-M/Pt) systems for ethane dehydrogenation using DFT calculations and kinetic Monte Carlo simulations. The results show that Ga2O3-Pt exhibits low ethylene formation activity (0.83 × 102 s–1) and selectivity (84.28%) due to its interfacial sites that weakly and uniformly adsorb hydrogen, impeding the differential regulation of key CH2CH3* intermediate adsorption behavior. Single-atom doping (M = Ti, Co, etc.) creates a Pt–M–O interfacial microenvironment, modulating the electronic structure of interfacial oxygen sites, which enables the effective differential regulation of CH2CH3* intermediate adsorption, thereby enhancing catalytic performance. Among the 14 screened dopants, the Ga2O3-Ti/Pt catalyst emerged as optimal, showing high activity (2.86 × 103 s–1) and selectivity (97.13%) for ethylene formation at the optimal 873.15 K and CH3CH3(g) partial pressure of 0.20 bar. This advantage stems from its moderate p-band center and Ti–O charge transfer, which yield an ideal hydrogen adsorption energy for CH2CH3* regulation. The H* adsorption energy can serve as a descriptor for qualitatively evaluating the activity of CH2CH2(g) formation for a series of Ga2O3-M/Pt catalysts. This work proposes the strategy of “interfacial microenvironment reconstruction to regulate the electronic structure” as a design method for developing high-efficiency alkane dehydrogenation catalysts.
nb131a1f9f242: The aqueous-phase hydrodeoxygenation of biomass-derived fatty acids offers an alternative route for the production of diesel-range hydrocarbons, but remains a major challenge. Herein, we report a hydrophobic CoP catalyst anchored on P–N co-doped carbon spheres (CoP@PNC-900), which exhibits high performance for the aqueous-phase hydrodeoxygenation of palmitic acid at 270 °C and 2 MPa H2, delivering nearly complete conversion together with over 99% yield of C15+C16 alkanes. The enhanced performance arises from the synergy between CoP active sites and the hydrophobic interface, which promotes C–O bond cleavage while enhancing the contact between hydrophobic substrates and catalytic sites. Isotopic-labeling experiments demonstrate that water acts exclusively as the reaction medium rather than a hydrogen source. In situ FT-IR–MS analysis combined with DFT calculations confirms the hydrodeoxygenation- and decarbonylation-related pathways, with C–O bond cleavage of the alcohol intermediate identified as the rate-determining step in the hydrodeoxygenation pathway. Moreover, the catalyst exhibits a broad substrate scope for various fatty acids and esters as well as stable recyclability under hydrothermal conditions. Finally, a preliminary life cycle assessment (LCA) highlights the potential environmental benefits of the aqueous-phase catalytic process. This work establishes an effective strategy that integrates active-site engineering with interfacial hydrophobic microenvironment regulation for the aqueous-phase valorization of biomass-derived fatty acids.
n6fc0a9500990: Ammonia synthesis under mild conditions remains challenging because of the inertness of the N≡N bond and the limited ability of conventional catalysts to couple efficient dinitrogen activation with rapid hydrogenation. Here, we report a LiH/FePcG catalyst in which strong interfacial coupling between LiH and Fe–N–C sites enable efficient ammonia synthesis. Comprehensive characterization, including structural analysis, kinetic study, isotopic-labelling, gas-phase mass spectrometry, and in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) reveal that the catalytic activity originates from interfacial active sites. Under reaction conditions, structural nitrogen atoms within the Fe–Nx moieties undergo reversible consumption and reconstruction, demonstrating the dynamic participation of the Fe–N–C framework in ammonia synthesis. Concurrently, hydridic hydrogen supplied by LiH directly participates in the initial hydrogenation steps, while the LiH/Fe–N–C interface generates Fe-centered multicomponent hydride species essential for N2 binding and activation. An inverse H/D kinetic isotope effect, an H2-promoted 28N2/30N2 exchange rate, in situ spectroscopic evidence, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations collectively support a non-classical, hydrogen-assisted pathway for dinitrogen activation rather than the conventional direct N≡ bond cleavage. These findings establish interfacial hydride chemistry as a cooperative mechanism for efficient ammonia synthesis and provide a strategy for designing advanced catalysts under mild conditions.
n95721645fcb9: Chemical looping oxidative dehydrogenation (CL-ODH) of ethane has emerged as a promising alternative for ethylene production, with the potential to mitigate the environmental and sustainability concerns associated with conventional steam cracking. The main challenge of CL-ODH is the design of active and selective redox catalysts to enhance ethane activation while minimizing the generation of by-products such as COx (CO and CO2). This study employs ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations to investigate the formation and reactivity of oxygen species in mixed metal-oxides@Li2CO3 and Na2CO3 redox catalysts. Estimated reaction free energies are used as thermodynamic descriptors, while the computational insights are supplemented with experimental validations. Our analysis indicates that peroxide (O22–) and •OH radicals provide more favorable thermodynamic driving forces for ethane C–H activation at the outer carbonate surface than monatomic oxygen radical anion (O–) and superoxide (O2–). In addition, mechanistic investigations into COx formation reveal that the product water can interact with peroxide-derived species at the gas–carbonate interface to generate •OH radicals, consistent with prior experimental observations. In Li2CO3, •OH-mediated pathways retain favorable ethane C─H activation thermodynamics while reducing the driving force for selected COx-forming transformations relative to peroxide. These findings provide important mechanistic insights into the design and optimization of mixed-oxide@alkali carbonate core-shell redox catalysts for CL-ODH.
n04f2e627a2d2: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction is a key reaction in nitrogen cycling and water remediation, yet the mechanistic interpretation of its voltammetric response remains poorly understood. On silver electrodes, cyclic voltammograms often display multiple cathodic features assigned to different reaction steps, although a consistent mechanistic interpretation remains elusive. Here, we combine cyclic voltammetry analysis with in situ product detection using scanning electrochemical microscopy (SECM), and hydrodynamic analysis using rotating disk electrode (RDE), to investigate nitrate-to-nitrite electroreduction on silver. We show that the cathodic response changes from a single peak to two distinct features with increasing nitrate concentration when using phosphate buffer as a supporting electrolyte. Analysis of concentration, scan rate, and pH dependencies, together with systematic variation of phosphate electrolyte composition, indicates that these features arise from distinct interfacial proton-transfer regimes associated with the availability of H2PO4– as a proton donor. In addition, SECM enables the assignment of each feature to local nitrite formation, ruling out changes in product identity as the origin of each feature. These findings show that phosphate electrolyte modulates proton-donor availability, and, consequently, the voltammetric response of nitrate reduction on silver, providing a framework for interpreting the complex electrocatalytic behavior observed in this system.
nb81153bd0fb6: Efficient methodologies for the catalytic asymmetric synthesis of α-aminophosphonic acid derivatives remain limited, particularly those involving carbon-carbon (C-C) bond formation. Herein, we report a copper(I)-catalyzed enantioselective alkylation of N-protected aminomethylthiophosphonates with alkyl halides, which provides a versatile strategy for accessing diverse chiral α-aminophosphonate derivatives. A wide range of alkyl halides, including allyl bromides, propargyl bromide, benzyl bromides, and alkyl iodides, act as efficient alkylating agents. Control experiments demonstrate that the employment of the 9H-fluoren-9-ylidene group and the incorporation of a sulfur atom into the phosphonate moiety are crucial for facilitating efficient deprotonation. NMR studies indicate that N-protected aminomethylthiophosphonate undergoes effective chelation with the copper(I) catalyst, a process that plays a pivotal role in promoting the reaction. Finally, both cleavage of the imine moiety and oxidation of the thiophosphonate group can be readily achieved under mild reaction conditions.
n0b352334afcf: Lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries are severely hindered by the shuttle effect of lithium polysulfides (LiPSs) and uncontrolled lithium dendrite growth. Herein, a defect-engineered MOF-303 (D-MOF-303) modified separator is developed via a ball-milling strategy to simultaneously mitigate both issues, marking the first application of MOF-303 in the Li–S battery field. The intentional introduction of ligand defects and oxygen vacancies reduces particle size, establishes a hierarchical porous structure, and amplifies local Lewis acidity. Consequently, the D-MOF-303 coating layer provides exceptional chemisorption and accelerated electrocatalytic conversion kinetics for LiPSs, while concurrently homogenizing lithium-ion flux to achieve long-term dendrite-free lithium plating. Benefiting from these synergistic merits, the resulting Li–S full cells exhibit high capacity retention over 500 cycles at 0.5 C, enhanced rate capability up to 3 C, and notable environmental resilience under high-humidity aging conditions. This work demonstrates the potential of coordination defect engineering in metal–organic frameworks for advancing high-energy-density and commercially viable energy storage technologies.
ne445f05af43a: Uranium contamination poses increasing environmental and health risks, yet the subcellular mechanisms underlying its toxicity and the protective effects of coexisting ions remain poorly understood. Here, by integrating cryo-SXT, transcriptomics, and physiological assays, we systematically decipher the multichannel protective mechanisms of calcium (Ca2+) against uranyl (UO22+) toxicity in Candida utilis, which act through metabolic reprogramming and biomineralization. In contrast, Ca2+ pretreatment effectively mitigates these lipotoxic effects by redirecting lipid flux to fatty acid β-oxidation. Concurrently, UO22+ triggers mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) loss, mitochondrial fragmentation, cristae disorganization, and downregulation of genes essential for cristae architecture and the electron transport chain (ETC). Such cellular disorders can be reversed by Ca2+, which restores reticular mitochondrial networks and cristae integrity. Furthermore, UO22+ enlarges the contact area between mitochondria and LDs, as well as between mitochondria and the nucleus, whereas Ca2+ pretreatment restores these contacts to near-normal levels. Notably, Ca2+ induces the accumulation of polyphosphate (polyP) within vacuoles and its subsequent mobilization to the cell wall, where it coprecipitates with UO22+ and Ca2+ to form stable extracellular calcium–uranium-phosphate nanoclusters. Collectively, this cross-scale imaging-omics strategy provides a mechanistic blueprint for cation-enhanced uranium tolerance and biomineralization, while also offering a transferable methodological framework for environmental toxicology.
n8f2e8c4d2b09: Acquired resistance to epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) poses a major clinical challenge for EGFR-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer patients with brain metastasis. To exploit this vulnerability, we developed MIL-S@M, a brain-targeted nanoplatform capable of efficient blood-brain barrier penetration and glutathione-responsive drug release. MIL-S@M potently induces ferroptosis through the synergistic effects of iron overload, glutathione depletion, and glutathione peroxidase 4 inactivation. In mouse models of osimertinib-resistant brain metastasis, MIL-S@M significantly suppressed tumor growth and extended survival, both as a monotherapy and in combination with osimertinib, without inducing systemic or neurotoxic effects. This work unveils a targetable adaptation in TKI-resistant brain metastasis and presents a translatable nanotherapeutic strategy.
n78190517042b: Quantum spin Hall insulators, also known as 2D topological insulators, are crucial 2D systems hosting topologically protected edge states. Here, we establish two-quintuple-layer Bi2Te3 and MnBi2Te4/Bi2Te3 heterostructures as atomically controlled, millimeter-scale 2D topological insulators, enabled by precision layer-by-layer growth that yields a carpet-like morphology extending coherently over macroscopic distances. This carpet-like growth mode renders the films amenable to mechanical exfoliation and subsequent wet or dry transfer. Multimodal spectroscopies and microscopies reveal the integer-layer-tuned electronic structure of (Bi2Te3)n in excellent agreement with theory. Photon-energy-dependent photoemission and time-resolved photoemission identify band inversion and band dynamics, respectively, while scanning tunneling spectroscopy resolves topological edge states that are characteristic of the 2D topological insulator phase. Thickness- and photon-energy-dependent photoemission further validate MnBi2Te4/Bi2Te3 as a robust 2D topological insulator. The large inverted gaps of ∼100 meV in (Bi2Te3)2 and ∼150 meV in MnBi2Te4/Bi2Te3 suggest operation near ambient temperature. These results define a scalable materials platform for next-generation, low-loss quantum and energy-efficient devices.
nf9478271f707: Respiratory viruses spread through aerosols and contaminated surfaces, yet masks, respirators, and filters only trap pathogens without inactivating them, turning used protective equipment into a secondary transmission source. Here, we report chiral ZnO nanoneedles (L-NNs or D-NNs), stabilized by L- or D-phenylalanine-penicillamine-phenylalanine (L-FPF or D-FPF), as a capture-and-kill coating that targets the heptad repeat 2 (HR2) of class I viral fusion proteins. Chiral ligands narrow the ZnO bandgap and, through chirality-induced spin selectivity that suppresses charge recombination, enable 405 nm light-driven proteolytic activity that hydrolyzes specific amide bonds between acidic and hydrophobic residues within HR2. n2e92a6c76ace: Spatial organization underpins efficient multistep catalysis in nature, yet recreating such organization on living cell surfaces using mild, enzyme-compatible and catalytically functional materials remains challenging. The coating maintains cell viability, enhances stress tolerance and provides size-selective permeability for small-molecule transport. SLF also incorporates exogenous enzymes efficiently during assembly. As a proof of concept, ω-transaminase-integrated SLF on G. oxydans couples host glycerol oxidation with surface transamination, enabling one-pot conversion of glycerol to serinol with a titer of 2.7 g L–1 within 12 h, up to 37-fold higher than a stepwise process. This work establishes ultrathin protein films as living catalytic interfaces for single-cell biocatalyst design and cascade biomanufacturing.
n9cafdbb4d3a7: Vanadium oxides are promising cathode materials for aqueous zinc ion batteries (ZIBs), but their practical application is hindered by low operating voltage and poor cycling stability.
